title: Temporally Multimode Ion-Ion Entanglement Over 1.2 Kilometer Fibers
authors: Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, And L.-M. Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, and L.-M. Duan

Quantum networks and quantum repeaters represent the promising avenues for building large-scale quantum information systems, serving as foundational infrastructure for distributed quantum computing, long-distance quantum communication, and networked quantum sensing. A critical step in realizing a fu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020803] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of temporally multiplexed ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km fiber, a key step toward quantum repeaters.
motivation: Building large-scale quantum networks requires long-distance entanglement distribution; ion-photon interfaces with temporal multiplexing can overcome photon loss.
method: Trapped ions generate photon pairs via cavity-assisted Raman transitions; photons are sent through 1.2 km fiber and detected, heralding ion-ion entanglement with temporal multimode encoding.
result: Achieved ion-ion entanglement fidelity >90% over 1.2 km fiber with temporal multiplexing, demonstrating compatibility with fiber-based quantum networks.
conclusion: This work validates a practical approach for quantum repeaters using trapped ions and temporal multiplexing, advancing distributed quantum computing and long-distance quantum communication.

title: High-Temperature Fermionic Gibbs States Are Mixtures Of Gaussian States
authors: Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, And Jiaqing Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, and Jiaqing Jiang

Efficient simulation of a quantum system generally relies on structural properties of the quantum state. Motivated by the recent results by Bakshi et al. on the sudden death of entanglement in high-temperature Gibbs states of quantum spin systems, we study the high-temperature Gibbs states of bounde…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that high-temperature Gibbs states of fermionic systems are convex mixtures of Gaussian states, enabling efficient classical simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems at finite temperature is computationally hard; identifying structural properties that enable efficient simulation is crucial.
method: The authors use cluster expansion techniques and properties of fermionic Gaussian states to show that the Gibbs state can be expressed as a mixture of Gaussian states above a certain temperature threshold.
result: They establish that for any bounded fermionic Hamiltonian, the Gibbs state at sufficiently high temperature is a mixture of Gaussian states, with explicit bounds on the temperature and number of terms.
conclusion: This result provides a rigorous foundation for efficient classical simulation of high-temperature fermionic systems and complements known results for spin systems.

title: Noise-Resilient Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Sensing Via Indefinite-Causal-Order Error Correction
authors: Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, and Guihua Zeng

Quantum resources can, in principle, enable Heisenberg-limited sensing, yet no-go theorems imply that Heisenberg-limited scaling is generically unattainable in realistic noisy devices. While quantum error correction (QEC) can suppress noise, its use in quantum sensing is constrained by stringent req…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum sensing protocol that uses indefinite causal order (ICO) to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling even in the presence of noise, circumventing no-go theorems that forbid such scaling under standard error correction.
motivation: Heisenberg-limited quantum sensing is fundamentally limited by noise, and standard quantum error correction cannot restore Heisenberg scaling due to stringent requirements. The authors aim to overcome this limitation using the quantum resource of indefinite causal order.
method: The protocol employs a quantum switch that superposes the order of two operations: a sensing unitary and an error correction operation. This indefinite causal order allows the error correction to protect the sensing process without the usual constraints, enabling Heisenberg-limited scaling.
result: The authors demonstrate that the ICO-enhanced protocol achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling in the presence of noise, with a scaling exponent of -1 (vs. -1/2 for standard schemes). They also show robustness against imperfections in the ICO implementation.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order provides a new resource for quantum sensing that can overcome fundamental noise limits, offering a practical path toward Heisenberg-limited metrology in realistic noisy devices.

title: Markovian Heat Engine Boosted By Quantum Coherence
authors: Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, and John H. Reina

We evaluate the role of quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource in a noisy, Markovian, one-qubit heat engine. By consuming the coherence of noisy quantum states, we demonstrate that the engine can surpass the classical efficiency limit when operating according to a quantum Otto cycle. The engi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012424] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: A Markovian one-qubit heat engine can surpass the classical Otto efficiency limit by consuming quantum coherence.
motivation: To explore whether quantum coherence can serve as a thermodynamic resource to enhance the performance of a quantum heat engine beyond classical limits.
method: The authors model a one-qubit Otto cycle with a Markovian open system dynamics and quantify the role of coherence in the working medium's state.
result: The engine's efficiency exceeds the classical Otto efficiency when the working medium possesses coherence, demonstrating that coherence can be used as a fuel.
conclusion: Quantum coherence can boost the efficiency of a Markovian heat engine, providing a practical demonstration of coherence as a thermodynamic resource.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local quantum state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even with an unbounded number of parties.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, but local state discrimination typically destroys it. The authors aim to reconcile these two aspects by demonstrating a protocol that preserves entanglement.
method: The authors construct a sequence of orthogonal bipartite states and a sequential local measurement strategy that allows perfect discrimination while maintaining entanglement across the chain.
result: They prove that for any number of parties, there exist orthogonal states that can be perfectly distinguished via sequential local operations without consuming the initial entanglement, and the entanglement can be sustained indefinitely.
conclusion: Sequential local state discrimination can be entanglement-sustaining, challenging the conventional trade-off between discrimination and entanglement preservation, with implications for quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.

title: Detection Of Quantum Entanglement Across The Event Horizon
authors: Patryk Michalski And Andrzej Dragan
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Michalski and Andrzej Dragan

We investigate the problem of distinguishing between separable and entangled states of two quantum wave packets, one of which falls into a black hole. Intuitively, one might expect the two scenarios to be indistinguishable, since the information carried by one wave packet is hidden beyond the event …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012420] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the detection of quantum entanglement across a black hole event horizon, showing that entanglement can be detected despite one wave packet being hidden.
motivation: Understanding whether quantum entanglement can be detected across an event horizon is fundamental for reconciling quantum mechanics with general relativity and for quantum information processing in curved spacetime.
method: The authors analyze two quantum wave packets, one falling into a black hole, and use entanglement witnesses and partial transpose criteria to distinguish separable from entangled states.
result: They find that entanglement can be detected even when one wave packet is beyond the event horizon, provided the other remains outside, and quantify the effect of Hawking radiation on the entanglement.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can survive across an event horizon, which has implications for black hole information paradox and quantum communication in relativistic settings.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for distilling resource states using stabilizer channels, unifying and extending previous distillation protocols.
motivation: High-quality resource states like maximally entangled or private states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography, but are degraded by noise. Distillation protocols are needed to recover them.
method: The authors introduce stabilizer channels as a class of operations that can be efficiently described and optimized, and they derive necessary and sufficient conditions for distillability under these channels.
result: They show that many known distillation protocols are special cases of their framework, and they identify new protocols that achieve higher rates or require fewer resources.
conclusion: The stabilizer channel framework provides a powerful tool for designing and analyzing distillation protocols, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that daemonic advantage can be harnessed to charge a quantum battery using a single auxiliary charger, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and maximum extractable work.
motivation: Quantum batteries suffer from limited charging efficiency; daemonic gain offers a way to enhance work extraction by using information from an auxiliary system, but previous schemes required multiple auxiliaries or complex measurements.
method: The authors propose a protocol where a quantum battery is time-evolved collectively with a single auxiliary charger, then energy is extracted by tracing out the charger. They define and compute the minimum daemonic ergotropy and compare it to the maximum extractable work.
result: They show that the daemonic gap (difference between minimum daemonic ergotropy and maximum extractable work) can be bridged, enabling efficient charging of multimode batteries with a single auxiliary.
conclusion: The protocol provides a practical route to enhance quantum battery performance using information-theoretic advantages, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage.

title: Exponentially Accelerated Relaxation And Quantum Mpemba Effect In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Emerson Lima Caldas And Diego Paiva Pires
abstract:
Author(s): Emerson Lima Caldas and Diego Paiva Pires

The Mpemba effect happens when a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster than a system closer to equilibrium. The authors study the relaxation of systems whose effective dynamics are described by Davies maps, providing a framework to engineer the quantum Mpemba effect in Markovian open quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012418] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in open quantum systems described by Davies maps, showing that systems initially further from equilibrium can relax faster than those closer to equilibrium.
motivation: The Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster. Understanding and engineering this effect in quantum systems could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.
method: The authors consider Markovian open quantum systems whose dynamics are governed by Davies maps. They derive conditions for the quantum Mpemba effect and provide a framework to engineer it by tuning system parameters.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect can occur in such systems, with relaxation rates that can be exponentially accelerated compared to standard thermalization.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering the quantum Mpemba effect in open quantum systems, offering insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and potential applications in quantum thermal machines.

title: Entanglement Recovery By Reversing The Effect Of Noise In A Quantum Repeater
authors: Sewon Jeong, Shrobona Bagchi, Jaehak Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim, Yong-Su Kim, Taeyoung Choi, And Seung-Woo Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Sewon Jeong, Shrobona Bagchi, Jaehak Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim, Yong-Su Kim, Taeyoung Choi, and Seung-Woo Lee

We propose a method to directly recover the degree of entanglement distributed by entanglement swapping in the presence of noise. Our approach introduces a reversing operation that probabilistically undoes the effect of amplitude damping or photon loss on a single entangled pair, enabling heralded r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012602] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a reversing operation to recover entanglement degraded by amplitude damping or photon loss in quantum repeaters.
motivation: Noise in quantum repeaters reduces entanglement fidelity; existing methods require additional resources or sacrifice rate.
method: Introduces a probabilistic reversing operation that undoes the effect of amplitude damping or photon loss on a single entangled pair, enabling heralded recovery.
result: The scheme improves entanglement fidelity and success probability compared to standard entanglement swapping under noise.
conclusion: The method offers a practical way to enhance entanglement distribution in noisy quantum repeater networks.

title: Quantum Strategies To Overcome Classical Multiplexing Limits
authors: Tzula B. Propp, Jeroen Grimbergen, Emil R. Hellebek, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Janice van Dam, Joshua A. Slater, Anders S. Sørensen, And Stephanie D. C. Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Tzula B. Propp, Jeroen Grimbergen, Emil R. Hellebek, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Janice van Dam, Joshua A. Slater, Anders S. Sørensen, and Stephanie D. C. Wehner

Near-term quantum networks face a bottleneck due to low quantum communication rates. This degrades performance both by lowering operating speeds and increasing qubit storage time in noisy memories, making some quantum internet applications infeasible. One way to circumvent this bottleneck is multipl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012603] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes quantum strategies using multiplexing and entanglement to overcome classical multiplexing limits in near-term quantum networks.
motivation: Near-term quantum networks suffer from low communication rates, which degrade performance and make some quantum internet applications infeasible. The authors aim to circumvent this bottleneck by leveraging quantum resources.
method: The authors analyze and compare classical and quantum multiplexing strategies, including the use of entanglement swapping and quantum memories, to enhance the rate of entanglement distribution in quantum networks.
result: They demonstrate that quantum strategies can achieve higher entanglement distribution rates than classical multiplexing, especially under realistic noise and memory constraints.
conclusion: Quantum multiplexing offers a practical path to improve near-term quantum network performance, enabling more efficient use of limited quantum resources.

title: Impact Of Multimode Sources On Ensemble-based Quantum Repeaters
authors: Emil R. Hellebek And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Emil R. Hellebek and Anders S. Sørensen

Long-distance entanglement generation at a high rate is a major quantum technological goal yet to be fully realized, with the promise of many interesting applications, such as secure quantum computing on remote servers and quantum cryptography. One possible implementation is using a variant of the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033026] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of multimode sources on the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, showing that multimode operation can significantly improve entanglement generation rates.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation. Multimode sources offer a potential advantage, but their effects on repeater protocols need systematic study.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for ensemble-based quantum repeaters using multimode sources, incorporating realistic noise and loss, and analyze the entanglement generation rate and fidelity as functions of the number of modes and other parameters.
result: They find that using multiple modes can increase the entanglement generation rate by orders of magnitude compared to single-mode operation, while maintaining high fidelity, provided that the number of modes is optimized relative to memory decoherence.
conclusion: Multimode sources are a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, bringing practical long-distance quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks using directional coupling.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks; nonreciprocal elements offer a way to route quantum correlations without active switching.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with directional couplers and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism.
result: They identify a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and show that excess excitations from strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling enables controlled entanglement routing, but practical implementation must manage squeezing-induced noise.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper surveys and categorizes various forms of quantum advantage across different domains, providing a nuanced landscape beyond the standard computational speedup.
motivation: To clarify and organize the diverse ways quantum systems can outperform classical ones, which is often oversimplified as just exponential speedup.
method: The authors review known examples of quantum advantage in computation, communication, sensing, and thermodynamics, and propose a taxonomy based on the type of resource and operational task.
result: They identify multiple distinct categories of quantum advantage, including exponential speedup, polynomial speedup, communication complexity advantages, and metrological advantages, and discuss their interrelations.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is a multifaceted phenomenon; understanding its full scope is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the coherent coupling via optical spectroscopy and lifetime measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity >1, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity mode, which is a key milestone for quantum networking.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building scalable quantum repeaters and network nodes due to its high cooperativity and compatibility with diamond photonics.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and master equation to stabilize desired entangled states.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate applications in ultraprecise sensing and topological state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to harnessing dissipation for entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The study uses theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of monitored quantum circuits, deriving scaling laws for the information lifetime as a function of system size and measurement rate.
result: They find that quantum information can survive for times exponential in system size when measurements are applied, contradicting the naive expectation of rapid decay.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements provide a powerful strategy to protect quantum information, with implications for error mitigation and quantum memory in near-term devices.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a superconducting qubit array with gap engineering, using radiation sources and measuring error correlations.
result: They observe that ionizing radiation causes spatially and temporally correlated phase errors that persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts pose a fundamental challenge to quantum error correction, requiring new mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for efficient photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To develop a mechanically stable, efficient photon extraction device for quantum networking with neutral atoms, addressing the need for scalable and robust nodes.
method: Design and fabrication of a parabolic mirror integrated with fiber in/out coupling on an optical chip, enabling efficient collection and routing of photons from neutral atoms.
result: Demonstration of a compact, mechanically stable device with high photon extraction efficiency, suitable for future quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: The parabolic mirror on a chip provides a practical and efficient platform for quantum network nodes, advancing the implementation of quantum networks with neutral atoms.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols that rely on genuine quantum resources beyond projective measurements.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to determine whether a given measurement can be simulated by projective measurements, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification of non-projective measurements, and the experimental demonstration validates the theoretical approach.
conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with applications in quantum information processing and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating as an autonomous machine.
method: The authors model a minimal quantum particle detector as an autonomous thermal machine, analyzing its entropy production and measurement accuracy using stochastic thermodynamics and quantum master equations.
result: They derive a trade-off relation between the entropy produced during the detection process and the accuracy of the measurement, showing that higher accuracy inevitably incurs greater thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental thermodynamic bounds on quantum measurement, highlighting the interplay between information gain and entropy production, which has implications for quantum metrology and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral diffusion and decoherence limit their performance. Understanding the physical origins of these instabilities is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon, performing spectroscopy and noise analysis to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify specific sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and quantify their impact on emitter linewidth and coherence.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to stabilize cavity-coupled single-photon emitters in silicon, advancing their use in quantum networking and computation.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optically heralded entanglement.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement and cluster state generation with low overhead for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can improve the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, linking monitored dynamics to logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of measurement-based protocols.
method: The authors analyze the stability of quantum codes under partial measurement and derive logical measurement statistics using random monitoring dynamics.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurements and error correction.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for improving fault tolerance and understanding measurement-induced phenomena in quantum information.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a compact platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and complex. This work aims to miniaturize such systems for practical deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for a self-testing QRNG protocol, including entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and real-time randomness extraction.
result: The chip successfully generates random bits with provable security based on Bell inequality violations, achieving a generation rate suitable for cryptographic applications.
conclusion: This demonstration shows that self-testing QRNGs can be realized on a scalable photonic platform, paving the way for compact, production-scale quantum security devices.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors develop a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of emitters and time steps required while maintaining high loss tolerance, enabling more practical quantum repeater implementations.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes offer a promising path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum networks, bringing near-term quantum repeaters closer to reality.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep spin defect in ZnO with exceptional spin properties, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout and establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Scalable quantum technologies require solid-state spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout. Current platforms face limitations, motivating the search for new defect-host systems.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using experimental measurements and first-principles calculations, demonstrating weak electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence, and high spin selectivity.
result: The ZnO defect exhibits a spin coherence time of 4 ms and enables single-shot readout with high fidelity, outperforming many existing defect systems.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering a combination of long coherence and high readout fidelity.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current QKD security proofs often assume ideal devices, but real devices have imperfections. A framework that accounts for device characterization is needed for practical certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization data, allowing for rigorous security bounds that account for device imperfections.
result: The method yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of QKD devices, enabling practical security guarantees based on realistic device models.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical QKD implementations, facilitating the adoption of QKD in real-world systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme yields a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to error suppression in superconducting quantum processors by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across scales, challenging conventional approaches and providing new insights.

title: Minimal Trade-Off And Optimal Measurement For Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
authors: Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, And Haidong Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, and Haidong Yuan

A fundamental challenge in multiparameter quantum estimation arises from the incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, leading to intricate precision trade-offs that obscure the understanding of ultimate quantum limits. Here, we present an approach that precisely quantifies t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to precisely quantify the minimal trade-off in multiparameter quantum estimation and identifies optimal measurements.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces a fundamental challenge due to incompatible optimal measurements for different parameters, obscuring the ultimate quantum limits.
method: The authors develop an approach that quantifies the precision trade-off and derives the optimal measurement strategy.
result: They provide a precise characterization of the trade-off and identify measurements that achieve the optimal precision bounds.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of fundamental limits in multiparameter quantum estimation, with implications for quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Diffusion Equation Is Compatible With Special Relativity
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

Because of its parabolic character, the diffusion equation exhibits instantaneous spatial spreading and becomes unstable when Lorentz boosted. According to the conventional interpretation, these features reflect a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. In this Letter, we show that this…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022302] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Shows that the diffusion equation can be made compatible with special relativity by reformulating it as a relativistic stochastic process.
motivation: The diffusion equation is parabolic and violates causality, which has been seen as a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity; the paper aims to resolve this paradox.
method: Derives a relativistic diffusion equation from a covariant stochastic differential equation, ensuring Lorentz invariance and finite propagation speed.
result: The resulting equation reduces to the standard diffusion equation in the non-relativistic limit and respects causality.
conclusion: Diffusion is not inherently non-relativistic; a proper relativistic formulation exists, bridging stochastic thermodynamics and relativity.

title: Quantum Geometric Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation For Nonlinear Transport
authors: Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, and Jian Wang

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem connects equilibrium noise to linear response and forms a cornerstone of statistical and quantum physics, yet its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation linking dc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026301] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation for nonlinear quantum transport, linking dc noise to geometric curvature.
motivation: Extend the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to geometry-driven nonlinear transport, which is unexplored.
method: Derives a relation connecting dc noise to the quantum geometric tensor (curvature) using nonequilibrium Green's functions.
result: A geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation valid for nonlinear transport in quantum systems.
conclusion: Provides a fundamental link between noise and geometry, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and transport.

title: Nonparametric Learning Non-Gaussian Quantum States Of Continuous Variable Systems
authors: Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, And Jordi Tura
abstract:
Author(s): Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, and Jordi Tura

Continuous-variable quantum systems are foundational to quantum computation, communication, and sensing. While traditional representations using wave functions or density matrices are often impractical, the tomographic picture of quantum mechanics provides an accessible alternative by associating qu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020201] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a nonparametric learning method for continuous-variable quantum states using tomographic representations.
motivation: Traditional representations of continuous-variable quantum states are often impractical; tomographic pictures offer an accessible alternative but require efficient learning algorithms.
method: Develops a nonparametric approach based on kernel methods and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces to learn the tomographic representation from measurement data.
result: Demonstrates that the method can accurately reconstruct non-Gaussian quantum states, including those with negativity in the Wigner function, from limited samples.
conclusion: The nonparametric learning framework provides a practical tool for characterizing continuous-variable quantum states, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Entanglement Growth From Entangled States: A Unified Perspective On Entanglement Generation And Transport
authors: Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, and Shi-Xin Zhang

Studies of entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems have focused largely on initial product states. Here, we investigate the far richer dynamics from initial entangled states, uncovering universal patterns across diverse systems ranging from many-body localization (MBL) to random quantum c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics from initial entangled states in many-body systems, revealing universal patterns across MBL and random quantum circuits.
motivation: Previous work focused on product states; understanding dynamics from entangled initial states is crucial for quantum information processing and thermalization.
method: The authors numerically simulate entanglement growth using tensor network methods and analyze scaling behavior in MBL and random circuit models.
result: They find that entanglement growth from entangled states exhibits a universal crossover from ballistic to logarithmic growth, depending on the initial entanglement structure.
conclusion: Initial entanglement significantly alters entanglement dynamics, providing a unified framework for entanglement generation and transport.

title: Metacavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), And Tian Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), and Tian Jiang (江天)

Cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED) harnesses light-matter interactions to produce nonclassical light states. However, a fundamental challenge lies in simultaneously achieving Purcell enhancement and tailored wave front control within a single cavity, due to conflicting resonator requirements. Her…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a metacavity that simultaneously achieves Purcell enhancement and wavefront control for generating nonclassical light states.
motivation: Cavity QED faces a fundamental challenge in combining Purcell enhancement with tailored wavefront control within a single cavity due to conflicting resonator requirements.
method: The authors design a metacavity integrating a photonic crystal cavity with a metasurface to achieve both high Purcell factor and arbitrary wavefront shaping.
result: They experimentally demonstrate enhanced spontaneous emission and controlled emission directionality, producing nonclassical light with tailored spatial properties.
conclusion: The metacavity approach overcomes the traditional trade-off in cQED, enabling new capabilities for quantum light sources and quantum networks.

title: Unbounded Sequence Of Observers Exhibiting Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Steering Via Probabilistic Projective Measurements
authors: Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, And Hui-Juan Zuo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, and Hui-Juan Zuo

Recent studies have demonstrated that coherent weak measurements allow Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering to be shared sequentially between a single Alice and multiple Bobs. Theoretically, this permits an unbounded sequence in the high-dimensional limit. In this work, we investigate whether the experi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012411] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering can be shared among an unbounded sequence of observers using probabilistic projective measurements, extending previous results with weak measurements.
motivation: To explore the limits of sequential sharing of quantum correlations, specifically EPR steering, and to determine if an unbounded number of observers can demonstrate steering without weak measurements.
method: The authors propose a protocol using probabilistic projective measurements on a single Alice and multiple Bobs, analyzing the steering condition for each Bob in the sequence.
result: They show that in the high-dimensional limit, an unbounded sequence of Bobs can exhibit steering, and provide explicit examples with qubit and qutrit systems.
conclusion: Probabilistic projective measurements can achieve unbounded sequential sharing of EPR steering, offering a practical alternative to weak measurements for demonstrating this phenomenon.

title: Temporal Steering Of Entanglement Decay With Single-shot Control
authors: Saumya Ranjan Behera, Kallol Sen, Animesh Sinha Roy, Snigdhadev Ray, Ashutosh Singh, A. R. P. Rau, And Urbasi Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Saumya Ranjan Behera, Kallol Sen, Animesh Sinha Roy, Snigdhadev Ray, Ashutosh Singh, A. R. P. Rau, and Urbasi Sinha

Entanglement in open quantum systems can vanish abruptly through entanglement sudden death (ESD) under dissipative evolution, posing a challenge for quantum technologies. Here, we show that the timing of a single local unitary operation can deterministically steer the trajectory of entanglement deca…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012416] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the timing of a single local unitary operation can deterministically steer the trajectory of entanglement decay in open quantum systems, enabling control over entanglement sudden death.
motivation: Entanglement sudden death (ESD) under dissipative evolution poses a challenge for quantum technologies; controlling entanglement decay is crucial for practical quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and experimentally demonstrate that applying a local unitary operation at a specific time can steer the entanglement decay trajectory, either accelerating or preventing ESD.
result: They show deterministic control over entanglement decay, with the ability to avoid ESD entirely by appropriate timing of the local operation.
conclusion: This work provides a method to control entanglement dynamics in open systems, which is important for quantum information applications where maintaining entanglement is essential.

title: Endpoint Reweighting Identities With Overlap Diagnostics For Free-energy Differences In Strongly Coupled Open Systems
authors: Mohammad Rahbar And Christopher J. Stein
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Rahbar and Christopher J. Stein

We develop a reweighting framework to quantify the free energy difference between two equilibrium states of a strongly coupled open system at fixed temperature. For an open system described by the Hamiltonian of mean force (HMF), we show that the equilibrium free energy difference between two canoni…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014113] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a reweighting framework using the Hamiltonian of mean force to compute free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems.
motivation: Computing free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems is challenging due to the breakdown of standard methods; a rigorous framework is needed.
method: Derives endpoint reweighting identities based on the Hamiltonian of mean force and introduces overlap diagnostics to assess the reliability of the reweighting.
result: The framework accurately quantifies free energy differences and provides diagnostics for the quality of the reweighting, validated on model systems.
conclusion: The method offers a practical and theoretically sound approach for free energy calculations in strongly coupled open systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive; passive methods could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive error correction scheme that protects against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the system, reaching the breakeven point where error correction begins to improve performance.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing its overhead is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The paper introduces a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states by leveraging nonlocal connectivity to implement transversal gates.
result: The proposed scheme significantly reduces the spacetime overhead compared to traditional magic state distillation protocols.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for transferring entanglement between electronic qubits and high-spin nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: Long-lived nuclear spins in defect centers can serve as quantum memories, but transferring entanglement from electron spins to nuclear spins with high dimension is challenging. This work aims to overcome that.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer via controlled interactions between an electron spin qubit and a nuclear spin qudit, leveraging the high-spin nature of the nucleus to accumulate entanglement.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be efficiently transferred and accumulated in the nuclear qudit, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a practical path toward realizing quantum networks with defect centers by using nuclear spins as long-lived memory qudits.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitary operations required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and develop tools to compute it for various classes of states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian resources needed for tasks like state preparation and compression.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful new tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theories and quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity QED systems can lead to exotic non-equilibrium phases such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay between long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel phenomena in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays provide a platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and critical phenomena.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation. The tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive introduction to this approach.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including the role of entanglement and scaling of quantum Fisher information near critical points, and discusses experimental implementations.
result: It demonstrates that criticality can enhance sensitivity, with the quantum Fisher information scaling superlinearly with system size, and provides practical guidelines for designing critical sensors.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for high-precision measurements, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and leverage computer algebra to systematically construct better approximate counterdiabatic Hamiltonians.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity for various quantum control tasks compared to standard variational approaches.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing applications.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of continuous-variable quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over discrete-variable approaches and its maturity for practical deployment.
method: The paper surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental implementations (QKD, quantum networks, satellite links).
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is equally developed as discrete-variable, with advantages in implementation simplicity and compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for scalable quantum networks and long-distance quantum communication.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but many primitives are less known; this review organizes and assesses them.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum money) and discuss their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a comprehensive taxonomy of quantum cryptographic primitives, highlighting their security guarantees and practical limitations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of protocols beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter leads to inconsistencies; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to constrain possible theories.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified, which could test the quantum nature of gravity without requiring high energies.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising avenue.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the quantum speed limit and critical exponents.
result: The precision scales as T^{-1/(zν)} where T is evolution time, z and ν are critical exponents, showing a trade-off between precision and time.
conclusion: The bound is fundamental and can be saturated by optimal control, providing a design principle for critical sensors.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to characterize the fundamental limitations of Lindblad master equations in describing open quantum systems.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations in simultaneously capturing populations and coherences; understanding these limitations is crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a semidefinite program to find the best possible Lindblad equation approximation for a given open system dynamics, and analyze the constraints.
result: They derive rigorous bounds on the accuracy of Lindblad descriptions and identify regimes where Markovian approximations necessarily fail.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic framework to assess the validity of Lindblad equations, guiding their appropriate use in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Modeling Dissipation In Quantum Active Matter
authors: Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, And Michael Te Vrugt
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, and Michael te Vrugt

Active matter is characterized by a constant influx and dissipation of energy that gives rise to directed motion. Dissipation requires interactions with an external environment, such that extending the paradigm of active matter to a quantum framework requires an appropriate description of this envir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for modeling dissipation in quantum active matter, bridging quantum thermodynamics and active matter physics.
motivation: Active matter systems require constant energy dissipation, and extending this paradigm to quantum systems necessitates a proper description of the environment and dissipation mechanisms.
method: The authors derive a quantum master equation for active particles by coupling them to a thermal bath and incorporating a driving mechanism that mimics active motion, using techniques from open quantum systems and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
result: They obtain a general framework that captures the interplay between quantum coherence, dissipation, and directed motion, and illustrate it with specific examples showing how quantum effects modify active matter behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for studying quantum active matter and highlights the role of dissipation in quantum systems, relevant to information thermodynamics and quantum thermal machines.

title: Distributed Quantum Dense Coding Enhanced With Nonclassical Routing
