Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and circuit depth for simulating linear differential equations, overcoming previous connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum algorithms and open system dynamics.

title: Black Hole States In Quantum Spin Chains
authors: Charlotte Kristjansen And Konstantin Zarembo
abstract:
Author(s): Charlotte Kristjansen and Konstantin Zarembo

We define a black hole state in a spin chain by studying thermal correlators in holography. Focusing on the Heisenberg model we investigate the thermal and complexity properties of the black hole state by evaluating its entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity. Th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021602] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines black hole states in spin chains using holography and studies their thermal and complexity properties.
motivation: To connect black hole physics with quantum spin chains via holographic duality, exploring thermalization and complexity in a tractable model.
method: Thermal correlators from holography are used to define a black hole state in the Heisenberg spin chain; entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity are computed.
result: The black hole state exhibits specific entanglement and complexity signatures that may reflect black hole properties.
conclusion: Spin chain black hole states provide a concrete model to study quantum aspects of black holes, though the connection to quantum information theory is indirect.

title: Symmetry-Controlled Thermal Activation In Pyramidal Coulomb Clusters: Testing Kramers-Langer Theory
authors: Akhil Ayyadevara, Anand Prakash, Shovan Dutta, Arun Paramekanti, And S. A. Rangwala
abstract:
Author(s): Akhil Ayyadevara, Anand Prakash, Shovan Dutta, Arun Paramekanti, and S. A. Rangwala

Laser-cooled ions confined in electromagnetic traps provide a unique, tunable mesoscopic system where the interplay of the trapping potential, nonlinear Coulomb interactions, and laser-ion scattering generates rich, collective dynamics. In this work, we engineer thermally activated switching between…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023002] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermally activated switching in laser-cooled ion Coulomb clusters, testing Kramers-Langer theory in a mesoscopic system.
motivation: Understanding thermal activation in small systems is important for thermodynamics at the nanoscale, but the paper focuses on classical stochastic dynamics rather than quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors engineer thermally activated switching between states in pyramidal Coulomb clusters of laser-cooled ions and compare the rates to Kramers-Langer theory.
result: They find that the switching rates follow Kramers-Langer theory with symmetry-controlled prefactors.
conclusion: The work provides a test of classical rate theory in a mesoscopic system but does not involve quantum information or quantum thermodynamics concepts.

title: Electromagnetically-induced-transparency Spectra Of A Ladder-type Four-level System With Quantum Frequency Mixing
authors: Sheng-Xian Xiao And Tao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng-Xian Xiao and Tao Wang

In this paper, we extend the quantum-frequency-mixing technology to a ladder-type four-level system and study its effect on electromagnetically-induced-transparency spectra. We find a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting in the probing field transmission spectra, which can be understood by…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012805] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum frequency mixing to a ladder-type four-level system and studies its effect on electromagnetically-induced-transparency (EIT) spectra, observing secondary Autler-Townes splitting.
motivation: To explore quantum frequency mixing in a more complex atomic system and understand its impact on EIT, which is relevant for quantum information processing and light-matter interfaces.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ladder-type four-level system driven by multiple fields, using quantum frequency mixing to modify the EIT spectrum, and derive the transmission spectra.
result: They find a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting in the probe field transmission spectra, which can be explained by the quantum frequency mixing process.
conclusion: Quantum frequency mixing can induce additional features in EIT spectra, potentially useful for controlling light propagation in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Noise-aware Quantum Architecture Search Based On A Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm
authors: Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, And Dazhi Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, and Dazhi Ding

Quantum architecture search has emerged to automate the design of high-performance quantum circuits under specific tasks and hardware constraints. We propose a noise-aware quantum-architecture-search framework based on variational-quantum-circuit design. By incorporating a noise model into the train…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012406] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A noise-aware quantum architecture search framework using a nondominated sorting genetic algorithm to design variational quantum circuits under hardware noise.
motivation: Automating the design of high-performance quantum circuits is challenging due to hardware noise and the vast search space.
method: The framework incorporates a noise model into the training process and uses a nondominated sorting genetic algorithm to optimize circuit architectures.
result: The proposed method yields circuits with improved fidelity and robustness to noise compared to manually designed circuits.
conclusion: Noise-aware architecture search can effectively produce quantum circuits that are both high-performing and noise-resilient.

title: Asymptotic Bounds On Quantum Partial Search Algorithm And Its Applications To Parallel Search
authors: Yan-Bo Jiang, Xiao-Hui Wang, Kun Zhang, And Vladimir Korepin
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Bo Jiang, Xiao-Hui Wang, Kun Zhang, and Vladimir Korepin

Grover's algorithm provides a quadratic speedup over classical algorithms for searching an unstructured database and is known to be strictly optimal in oracle query complexity, with tight bounds on its success probability. Although the standard Grover search cannot be further accelerated in the full…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012412] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives asymptotic bounds on the success probability of a quantum partial search algorithm and extends it to parallel search, showing that the partial search can achieve the same query complexity as full Grover search.
motivation: Grover's algorithm is optimal for full search, but partial search (finding a target in a subset of the database) may have different bounds. The authors aim to characterize the asymptotic behavior and explore applications to parallel search.
method: The authors analyze the quantum partial search algorithm using the quantum walk framework and derive tight asymptotic bounds on the success probability. They then generalize to parallel search where multiple targets are sought simultaneously.
result: They prove that the partial search algorithm can achieve success probability arbitrarily close to 1 with the same query complexity as full Grover search, and the parallel search version maintains the quadratic speedup.
conclusion: The results show that partial search does not incur additional overhead compared to full search, and the parallel extension is efficient for multiple targets.

title: Limitations For Adaptive Quantum State Tomography In The Presence Of Detector Noise
authors: Adrian Skasberg Aasen And Martin Gärttner
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Skasberg Aasen and Martin Gärttner

Assumption-free reconstruction of quantum states from measurements is essential for benchmarking and certifying quantum devices, but it remains difficult due to the extensive measurement statistics and experimental resources it demands. An approach to alleviating these demands is provided by adaptiv…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012414] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the limitations of adaptive quantum state tomography under detector noise, showing that noise reduces the advantage of adaptivity.
motivation: Adaptive quantum state tomography can reduce measurement resources, but its performance in the presence of realistic detector noise is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the Fisher information and Bayesian inference for adaptive tomography protocols with noisy detectors, deriving bounds on achievable precision.
result: Detector noise significantly degrades the advantage of adaptive over non-adaptive tomography, and in some regimes adaptivity provides no benefit.
conclusion: Practical adaptive tomography must account for detector imperfections, and noise-aware protocols may be needed to regain advantages.

title: Energy-time Attack On Detectors In Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Konstantin Zaitsev, Vladimir Bizin, Dmitriy Kuzmin, And Vadim Makarov
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantin Zaitsev, Vladimir Bizin, Dmitriy Kuzmin, and Vadim Makarov

Quantum key distribution is unbreakable in theory but may be hacked via imperfections in its hardware implementations. While many imperfections have been mitigated by countermeasures and advanced security proofs, several remain unsolved. One of these is a superlinear behavior in single-photon detect…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012601] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an energy-time attack on single-photon detectors in QKD systems, exploiting superlinear detection behavior to compromise security.
motivation: Quantum key distribution is theoretically secure but hardware imperfections can be exploited; this work addresses a specific detector vulnerability that remains unsolved.
method: The authors demonstrate an attack that uses energy-time correlations to manipulate detector responses, bypassing standard countermeasures.
result: The attack successfully compromises the security of QKD implementations by exploiting superlinear detector behavior, showing that current countermeasures are insufficient.
conclusion: New countermeasures are needed to protect QKD detectors against energy-time side-channel attacks.

title: Physically Motivated Decompositions Of Single-qutrit Gates
authors: Aryan Iliat, Mark Byrd, Sahel Ashhab, And Lian-Ao Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Aryan Iliat, Mark Byrd, Sahel Ashhab, and Lian-Ao Wu

Although only two quantum states of a physical system are often used to encode quantum information into qubits, in principle, qudits (a system with a number [MATH] states) could be used to increase the information capacity of the system. In this work, three-state systems (qutrits) are studied using a p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012606] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents physically motivated decompositions of single-qutrit gates using a parameterization based on angular momentum operators.
motivation: Qudits offer higher information capacity than qubits, but gate decompositions for qutrits are less developed. The authors aim to provide intuitive decompositions that connect to physical implementations.
method: The authors parameterize single-qutrit gates using angular momentum operators and derive decompositions into rotations and phase gates, analogous to qubit Euler angles.
result: They obtain explicit decompositions for arbitrary single-qutrit gates in terms of physically realizable operations, with applications to specific gate families.
conclusion: The decompositions facilitate the design and control of qutrit-based quantum processors, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Riding The Wave: Polymers In Time-dependent Nonequilibrium Baths
authors: Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, And Abhinav Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, and Abhinav Sharma

Directed transport is a characteristic feature of numerous biological systems in response to signals such as nutrient and chemical gradients. These signals often depend on time owing to the high complexity of interactions in these systems. In this study, we focus on the steady-state behavior of poly…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015408] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies directed transport of polymers in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths, focusing on steady-state behavior.
motivation: Understanding directed transport in biological systems where signals are time-dependent due to complex interactions.
method: Theoretical analysis of polymer dynamics in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths, likely using stochastic thermodynamics or polymer physics.
result: Steady-state behavior of polymers under time-dependent driving is characterized.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium transport in biological systems, but is more applied and less directly relevant to quantum information thermodynamics.

title: Violation Of The Fluctuation Dissipation Theorem During Domain Growth In The Long-range Ising Model
authors: Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, And Varsha Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, and Varsha Banerjee

The celebrated fluctuation dissipation theorem (FDT) does not apply to nonequilibrium systems. In this context, Cugliandolo and Kurchan [
tldr: This paper studies the violation of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem during domain growth in the long-range Ising model, providing a generalized FDT framework for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: The fluctuation-dissipation theorem does not hold in nonequilibrium systems, and understanding its violation is crucial for characterizing aging and coarsening dynamics.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of the long-range Ising model with power-law interactions and analyze the two-time correlation and response functions to extract the violation factor.
result: They find that the violation factor exhibits a scaling behavior that depends on the range of interactions, and the generalized FDT holds with a time-dependent effective temperature.
conclusion: The study extends the understanding of FDT violation to long-range interacting systems, showing that the effective temperature concept remains valid but with modified scaling.

title: Learning Complexity Gradually In Quantum Machine Learning Models
authors: Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, And Carlos Bravo-Prieto
abstract:
Author(s): Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, and Carlos Bravo-Prieto

Quantum machine learning is an emergent field that continues to draw significant interest for its potential to offer improvements over classical algorithms in certain areas. However, training quantum models remains a challenging task, largely because of the difficulty in establishing an effective in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033006] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gradual training strategy for quantum machine learning models to mitigate barren plateaus and improve trainability.
motivation: Training quantum models is challenging due to barren plateaus and difficulty in establishing effective initialization strategies.
method: The authors introduce a method that gradually increases the expressivity of the quantum model during training, starting from a simpler model and progressively adding complexity.
result: The gradual training approach helps avoid barren plateaus and leads to better convergence and performance compared to standard training.
conclusion: Gradual complexity increase is a promising technique for improving trainability in quantum machine learning, though it is more of a practical heuristic than a fundamental information-theoretic result.

title: Learning Minimal Representations Of Fermionic Ground States
authors: Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, And Stefano Polla
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, and Stefano Polla

We introduce an unsupervised machine-learning framework that discovers optimally compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states. Using an autoencoder neural network architecture on reduced density matrix data from [MATH]-site Fermi-Hubbard models, we identify minimal latent spaces with a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033014] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised machine learning framework using autoencoders to learn minimal representations of fermionic ground states from reduced density matrix data.
motivation: To discover optimally compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states, which can aid in understanding and simulating complex quantum systems.
method: Applied an autoencoder neural network to reduced density matrix data from Fermi-Hubbard models to identify minimal latent spaces.
result: The framework successfully identified minimal representations that capture essential features of the ground states.
conclusion: The approach provides a data-driven method for compressing quantum many-body states, potentially useful for quantum information tasks.

title: Variational Matrix Product States For Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Guillermo Preisser, Conor Mc Keever, And Michael Lubasch
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Preisser, Conor Mc Keever, and Michael Lubasch

To compute approximate solutions for combinatorial optimization problems, we describe variational methods based on the product state (PS) and matrix product state (MPS) ansätze. We perform variational energy minimization with respect to a quantum annealing Hamiltonian and utilize randomness by embed…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033027] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies variational matrix product states to solve combinatorial optimization problems via quantum annealing.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization is important but hard; quantum annealing offers a potential advantage, but classical simulation of quantum systems is challenging.
method: The authors use variational energy minimization with product state and matrix product state ansätze, embedding the optimization problem into a quantum annealing Hamiltonian.
result: The variational MPS method achieves competitive approximate solutions for several benchmark problems, demonstrating scalability and accuracy.
conclusion: Variational MPS provide a classical simulation tool for quantum annealing that can yield good approximate solutions to combinatorial optimization problems.

title: Complexity And Multifunctional Variants Of The Quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli Factories
authors: Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, And Fabio Sciarrino
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, and Fabio Sciarrino

A Bernoulli factory is a model for randomness manipulation that transforms an initial Bernoulli random variable into another Bernoulli variable by applying a predetermined function relating the output bias to the input one. In literature, quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes have been propos…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033003] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factories, introducing complex and multifunctional variants that leverage quantum resources for randomness manipulation.
motivation: Bernoulli factories are a model for randomness manipulation; extending them to the quantum domain could enable new quantum information processing tasks.
method: The authors propose and analyze quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes using quantum states and operations, demonstrating multifunctional capabilities.
result: They show that quantum resources allow for more complex and versatile Bernoulli factories compared to classical ones.
conclusion: Quantum Bernoulli factories represent a novel application of quantum information, but the work is more of a niche extension rather than a breakthrough in core quantum information theory.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for optimizing optical quantum state generation, significantly increasing success rates.
motivation: Generating non-Gaussian quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods suffer from low success rates. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: The authors propose control parameters beyond the stellar rank to characterize and optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems, using theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success probability of generating essential non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for scalable optical quantum state engineering, advancing quantum information applications.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks, showing that they maintain learning ability as parameters grow, unlike classical networks.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from loss of plasticity (inability to learn new tasks) as they grow, and this work explores whether quantum neural networks can overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and experimentally demonstrate that quantum neural networks retain plasticity due to the structure of quantum parameter space, using continual learning benchmarks.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit sustained learning capability over many tasks without explicit plasticity preservation techniques, outperforming classical counterparts.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks offer a natural advantage for continual learning, which could be leveraged for more adaptive AI systems.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, including mapping to statistical mechanics models and analyzing the spectral properties of the noise-averaged circuit.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth that scales logarithmically with system size, after which it is lost. The behavior is universal across different circuit architectures and noise models.
conclusion: Noisy random circuits exhibit a universal anticoncentration transition, which sets fundamental limits on quantum advantage experiments and informs the design of near-term quantum devices.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than direct information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity across regimes, highlighting where quantum computers may outperform classical ones.
conclusion: The work offers insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function problems, but is more aligned with quantum complexity theory than core quantum information topics.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become inefficient for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the reach of such methods by exploiting symmetries.
method: The authors develop a framework that combines strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling simulation of circuits that were previously beyond reach.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach can simulate Clifford-dominated circuits with significantly more non-Clifford gates than previous methods, providing concrete complexity improvements.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is a powerful tool for classical simulation of quantum circuits, and the proposed techniques expand the regime where stabilizer-based methods are effective.

title: Quantum-Error-Correction-Inspired Noise Mitigation For Wavelike Dark Matter Searches With Quantum Sensors
authors: Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, And Thanaporn Sichanugrist
abstract:
Author(s): Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, and Thanaporn Sichanugrist

We propose a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol for enhancing the sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches with quantum sensors. Our protocol uses multiple sensors to mitigate the noise affecting each sensor individually, allowing for the suppression of excitation noise …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol to enhance sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches using quantum sensors.
motivation: Dark matter searches with quantum sensors are limited by noise; improving sensitivity is crucial for detection.
method: Uses multiple quantum sensors and a noise mitigation protocol inspired by quantum error correction to suppress individual sensor noise.
result: The protocol enhances sensitivity for wavelike dark matter detection beyond standard approaches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction techniques can be adapted to improve quantum sensor performance in fundamental physics searches.

title: How Lorentz Boosts Reshape Relaxation Spectra
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

In relativity, relaxation processes are often assumed to undergo time dilation under Lorentz boosts. We show that this intuition fails generically. Because of relativity of simultaneity, Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, with a width set by the maxima…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, challenging the naive expectation of time dilation for relaxation processes.
motivation: To understand how relativistic effects, specifically Lorentz boosts, modify relaxation spectra, which is important for relativistic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The author uses relativistic kinetic theory and field-theoretic arguments to analyze the transformation of relaxation modes under Lorentz boosts, deriving the resulting spectral broadening.
result: Lorentz boosts generically convert a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations with a width set by the maximum boost factor, contradicting simple time dilation.
conclusion: Relaxation processes in relativity are more complex than previously thought, with implications for relativistic fluid dynamics and the thermodynamics of moving systems.

title: Free-fermion Measurement-induced Volume- To Area-law Entanglement Transition In The Presence Of Fermion Interactions
authors: Matthew S. Foster, Haoyu Guo, Chao-Ming Jian, And Andreas W. W. Ludwig
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew S. Foster, Haoyu Guo, Chao-Ming Jian, and Andreas W. W. Ludwig

In quantum many-body systems, chaotic dynamics that explore all configurations can give way to a localized phase, frozen into a small corner of possibilities. These phases are distinguished by the extensivity of entanglement. Here, the authors argue that the entanglement transition driven by measurements in a broad class of interacting quantum circuits can be described by ree ermions, and they develop a controlled description of the transition via non-Abelian bosonization. The results are also relevant to decodability transitions in certain surface codes with coherent errors.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024306] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies measurement-induced entanglement transitions in interacting fermion systems, mapping them to free-fermion transitions via non-Abelian bosonization.
motivation: Understanding measurement-induced phase transitions in many-body quantum systems is a key challenge, especially in the presence of interactions.
method: The authors use non-Abelian bosonization to map the interacting problem to a free-fermion description, enabling controlled analysis of the entanglement transition.
result: They show that the measurement-induced volume-to-area law entanglement transition in a class of interacting quantum circuits can be described by free fermions.
conclusion: The results provide a tractable framework for measurement-induced transitions and have implications for decodability transitions in surface codes with coherent errors.

title: Transient Triplet Blockade In Andreev Junction
authors: R. Taranko, J. Barański, A. Jankiewicz, K. Wrześniewski, I. Weymann, And T. Domański
abstract:
Author(s): R. Taranko, J. Barański, A. Jankiewicz, K. Wrześniewski, I. Weymann, and T. Domański

We study the time-dependent triplet configuration, appearing under nonequilibrium conditions in a nanoscopic junction with two quantum dots (QDs) coupled in series between superconductor and normal metallic lead. We show that, in the situation when both QDs are singly occupied by identical spin elec…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045407] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transient triplet blockade in a superconductor-quantum dot junction under nonequilibrium conditions.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of triplet configurations in nanoscopic junctions, which is relevant for spintronics and quantum transport.
method: The authors use a theoretical model of two quantum dots coupled in series between a superconductor and a normal lead, analyzing time-dependent triplet formation.
result: They show that a transient triplet blockade occurs under certain nonequilibrium conditions, affecting the current.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into spin-dependent transport in hybrid superconducting devices.

title: Metastability, Chaos, And Spectrum Tomography For Bose-Hubbard Rings And Chains
authors: Rajat And Doron Cohen
abstract:
Author(s): Rajat and Doron Cohen

We analyze the metastability of Bose-Hubbard condensates for finite-size one-dimensional ring lattices and open chains, using a semiclassical tomographic perspective that emphasizes the relation of the many-body spectrum to the underlying classical phase-space structures. In order to address quantum…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033024] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes metastability and chaos in Bose-Hubbard rings and chains using semiclassical tomography, linking many-body spectrum to classical phase-space structures.
motivation: Understanding metastability and chaos in finite-size Bose-Hubbard systems is important for quantum many-body physics, but the paper does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information.
method: The authors use a semiclassical tomographic approach to relate the many-body quantum spectrum to classical phase-space structures, analyzing metastability and chaos.
result: They find that metastability and chaos are connected to the underlying classical dynamics, and they develop a spectrum tomography method.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the quantum-classical correspondence in Bose-Hubbard systems, but its relevance to information thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in two dimensions is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing logical gates without braiding. The authors aim to overcome this by leveraging non-Abelian phases.
method: The method involves temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform complex logic gates, enabling universal computation without braiding.
result: The authors demonstrate a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using this approach.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing that avoids the need for braiding, potentially simplifying experimental implementations.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires high overhead; the goal is to reduce both qubit and time overhead using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques with good quantum LDPC codes to achieve efficient fault tolerance.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, significantly improving over conventional surface code approaches.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes enable more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation, bringing practical quantum computing closer.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes is proposed to achieve high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements.
method: The authors design a beam search algorithm tailored to quantum LDPC codes, which explores multiple candidate error patterns in parallel to find the most likely correction.
result: The beam search decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency constraints for real-time quantum error correction, avoiding the need for massive classical computation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes that balances accuracy and speed, advancing real-time quantum error correction.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using twisted color circuits and a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient non-Clifford gates, which are challenging on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits, a family of scalable circuits designed for planar chips, combined with a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed circuits can implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code with a planar layout.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar chips, though the focus is on hardware-level error correction rather than information-theoretic results.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting quantum-dot systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments suggest Majorana bound states may exist, but their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing in interacting systems need rigorous quantification.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality using numerical simulations.
result: They provide quantitative bounds on the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states, showing how interactions affect their topological protection.
conclusion: The work clarifies conditions under which Majorana bound states can be used for non-Abelian braiding, guiding experimental efforts in quantum-dot platforms.

title: Mixed Phases In Feedback Ising Models
authors: Yi-Ping Ma, Ivan Sudakow, And P. L. Krapivsky
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ping Ma, Ivan Sudakow, and P. L. Krapivsky

We study mean-field Ising models in which the coupling depends on the magnetization via a feedback function. We identify mixed phases (MPs) and show that they can be stable at zero temperature for sufficiently strong feedback. Moreover, stable MPs are always superstable, meaning that perturbations d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 027101] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mean-field Ising models with feedback-dependent coupling, identifying stable mixed phases at zero temperature.
motivation: To understand how feedback mechanisms in statistical mechanics models can lead to novel phases beyond standard equilibrium behavior.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of mean-field Ising models with a feedback function coupling to magnetization.
result: Mixed phases are stable at zero temperature for sufficiently strong feedback and are superstable, meaning perturbations decay exponentially.
conclusion: Feedback can stabilize mixed phases in Ising models, which may have implications for understanding complex systems with feedback.

title: Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Dimers In Rydberg Atom Chains
authors: Feng-Yuan Kuang, Lin Li, And Weibin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Feng-Yuan Kuang, Lin Li, and Weibin Li

We investigate the dynamics of antiferromagnetic dimers within a Rydberg atom chain in the regime where laser detuning compensates for nearest-neighbor (NN) interactions. Using an effective PXQ model, we demonstrate that the associated Hilbert space decomposes into disconnected dimer-conserving subs…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013309] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic dimers in a Rydberg atom chain using an effective PXQ model, revealing dimer-conserving subspaces and constrained dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of Rydberg atom chains is important for quantum simulation and many-body physics, but the paper focuses on a specific model of antiferromagnetic dimers rather than core quantum information topics.
method: The authors derive an effective PXQ model for the Rydberg atom chain and analyze the Hilbert space decomposition into dimer-conserving subspaces.
result: They demonstrate that the dynamics are constrained within these subspaces, leading to non-ergodic behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into constrained dynamics in Rydberg systems but does not directly advance quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Integrability From A Single Conservation Law In Quantum Spin Chains
authors: Akihiro Hokkyo
abstract:
Author(s): Akihiro Hokkyo

Here, the author proves that, for translationally invariant spin chains with finite-range interactions, a single third-order conservation law is enough to guarantee infinitely many commuting local conserved quantities. This result turns the Reshetikhin condition from a widely used heuristic into a rigorous sufficient criterion for quantum integrability and helps clarify the divide between integrable and nonintegrable many-body systems.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055108] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Proves that a single third-order conservation law implies infinite commuting local conserved quantities in translationally invariant spin chains, establishing a rigorous criterion for quantum integrability.
motivation: Quantum integrability is often assumed based on heuristic criteria; this work aims to provide a rigorous sufficient condition to distinguish integrable from nonintegrable many-body systems.
method: The author proves that for translationally invariant spin chains with finite-range interactions, the existence of a third-order local conserved quantity guarantees an infinite hierarchy of commuting local conserved quantities, using algebraic and combinatorial arguments.
result: The Reshetikhin condition is shown to be a sufficient criterion for quantum integrability, rigorously establishing that a single higher-order conservation law leads to full integrability.
conclusion: This result clarifies the divide between integrable and nonintegrable quantum many-body systems and provides a practical tool for identifying integrable models.

title: Triggering Of The Manganese Spin Precession In (Cd,Mn)Te/(Cd,Mg)Te Quantum Wells By The Inverse Faraday Effect
authors: E. A. Zhukov, V. N. Mantsevich, V. V. Nedelea, N. V. Kozyrev, B. R. Namozov, Yu. G. Kusrayev, I. A. Akimov, D. R. Yakovlev, G. Karczewski, And M. Bayer
abstract:
Author(s): E. A. Zhukov, V. N. Mantsevich, V. V. Nedelea, N. V. Kozyrev, B. R. Namozov, Yu. G. Kusrayev, I. A. Akimov, D. R. Yakovlev, G. Karczewski, and M. Bayer

Coherent spin dynamics of localized [MATH] spins are studied in a single (Cd,Mn)Te/(Cd,Mg)Te diluted-magnetic-semiconductor quantum well using a two-color pump-probe Faraday rotation technique. The initial phase of the manganese Larmor precession in magnetic field is measured at the ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065302] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coherent spin dynamics of Mn ions in diluted magnetic semiconductor quantum wells using pump-probe Faraday rotation, focusing on the initial phase of Larmor precession triggered by the inverse Faraday effect.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin dynamics in diluted magnetic semiconductors is important for spintronics and quantum information processing, but this work is primarily a materials characterization study.
method: A two-color pump-probe Faraday rotation technique is used to measure the initial phase of manganese Larmor precession in a (Cd,Mn)Te/(Cd,Mg)Te quantum well under magnetic field.
result: The initial phase of the Mn spin precession is measured and analyzed, revealing the triggering mechanism via the inverse Faraday effect.
conclusion: The study provides insights into coherent spin dynamics of Mn ions, but does not directly advance quantum information or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Toric Code Under Antiferromagnetic Isotropic Heisenberg Interactions
authors: Won Jang, Robert Peters, And Thore Posske
abstract:
Author(s): Won Jang, Robert Peters, and Thore Posske

We investigate the impact of an isotropic antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, focusing on the resulting quantum phase transition and the nature of the phase that emerges beyond topological order. Using neural-network quantum states, we compute ground states over a wide range…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033008] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of an antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, revealing a quantum phase transition to a trivial paramagnet.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of topological order in the toric code under perturbations is important for quantum error correction and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use neural-network quantum states (NQS) to compute ground states and analyze the phase transition via order parameters and entanglement entropy.
result: They find a direct first-order phase transition from the topological phase to a trivial paramagnet, with no intermediate phase.
conclusion: The toric code's topological order is fragile against isotropic Heisenberg interactions, and the transition is first-order.

title: Stable Infinite-temperature Eigenstates In SU(2)-symmetric Nonintegrable Models
authors: Christopher J. Turner, Marcin Szyniszewski, Bhaskar Mukherjee, Ronald Melendrez, Hitesh J. Changlani, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher J. Turner, Marcin Szyniszewski, Bhaskar Mukherjee, Ronald Melendrez, Hitesh J. Changlani, and Arijeet Pal

Spectral properties and zero-energy degeneracy provide a way to characterize thermalization in nonintegrable quantum many-body systems. This work studies a bond-staggered Heisenberg chain with spectral reflection symmetry and continuous non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry, using character theory to count exponentially many zero-energy states and constructing exact low-entangled few-magnon eigenstates that are stable under many perturbations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022064] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stable infinite-temperature eigenstates in a SU(2)-symmetric nonintegrable Heisenberg chain, focusing on spectral properties and thermalization.
motivation: Understanding thermalization in nonintegrable quantum many-body systems is a key goal; here the authors aim to characterize zero-energy degeneracy and construct exact eigenstates that evade thermalization.
method: Using character theory to count zero-energy states and constructing exact low-entangled few-magnon eigenstates in a bond-staggered Heisenberg chain with SU(2) symmetry.
result: Exponentially many zero-energy states are found, and exact eigenstates are stable under many perturbations, indicating a violation of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
conclusion: The work reveals a mechanism for non-thermalizing eigenstates in a nonintegrable model, which may have implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement with error correction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation that allows multiple Pauli products to be commuted through T gates, enabling more efficient circuit compilation.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for optimizing quantum circuits, contributing to the practical realization of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The paper reviews the use of maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to model the electrical activity of thousands of simultaneously recorded neurons.
result: These statistical physics approaches uncover quantitatively reproducible behaviors in neural data, bridging theory and experiment.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from statistical physics can achieve predictive power in neuroscience comparable to other areas of physics.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Highlights key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Low-frequency Electric Field Sensing With A Rydberg Beam
authors: Jeremy Glick, John R. Dickson, Josie Wood, And Paul Kunz
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy Glick, John R. Dickson, Josie Wood, and Paul Kunz

The authors perform low-frequency electric field sensing using ionization detection on a collimated beam of Rydberg atoms. This reduces challenges associated with electric field screening effects present in warm vapor cells containing alkali-metal atoms.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012608] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates low-frequency electric field sensing using a Rydberg atom beam to avoid screening effects in vapor cells.
motivation: Low-frequency electric field sensing is important for various applications, but traditional Rydberg atom vapor cells suffer from electric field screening due to dielectric walls and stray charges.
method: The authors use a collimated beam of Rydberg atoms and detect ionization to measure electric fields, which reduces screening effects present in warm vapor cells.
result: The beam-based approach enables sensitive detection of low-frequency electric fields with reduced systematic errors from screening.
conclusion: Rydberg atom beams offer a promising platform for low-frequency electric field sensing, overcoming limitations of vapor cell techniques.

title: Multiple Majorana Zero Modes Induced By Geometric Spin-orbit Coupling In Helical Nanoribbon-superconductor Hybrids
authors: Kai-Yuan Zhang, Shu-Zheng Zhou, Xi Sun, And Hua-Hua Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Yuan Zhang, Shu-Zheng Zhou, Xi Sun, and Hua-Hua Fu

Majorana zero modes (MZMs), which serve as a key platform for realizing fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, remain challenging in excitation and regulation. In this work, we propose chiral nanoribbon-superconductor hybrids as a platform for realizing multiple MZMs. The hybrid system compri…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065408] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a chiral nanoribbon-superconductor hybrid platform to realize multiple Majorana zero modes via geometric spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: Majorana zero modes are promising for fault-tolerant topological quantum computing but remain difficult to excite and control. The authors aim to design a new platform that can host multiple MZMs.
method: The hybrid system consists of a helical nanoribbon with geometric spin-orbit coupling placed on a superconductor. The authors theoretically analyze the electronic structure and topological properties using a tight-binding model and calculate the resulting Majorana modes.
result: Multiple Majorana zero modes are predicted to appear at the ends of the nanoribbon, with their number and stability tunable by the spin-orbit coupling strength and ribbon geometry.
conclusion: The proposed platform offers a controllable way to generate multiple MZMs, potentially advancing topological quantum computing, though experimental realization remains challenging.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the relationship between space-time duality and integrable quantum circuits.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.
