method: The authors introduce Euclidean defects into hyperbolic lattices and compute the two-point boundary correlation function and density of states using tight-binding models.
result: They observe a crossover in the density of states and boundary correlations as defects are added, interpolating between hyperbolic and Euclidean behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into discrete holography and the interplay between lattice geometry and quantum properties, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Probing Imbalanced Weyl Nodes In A Two-dimensional Anisotropic Semimetal Via Optical Conductivity
authors: Suheel Ahmad Malik, M. A. H. Ahsan, And SK Firoz Islam
abstract:
Author(s): Suheel Ahmad Malik, M. A. H. Ahsan, and SK Firoz Islam

We present a theoretical investigation of the electronic band structure and optical properties of a two-dimensional anisotropic semimetal described by a tilted semi-Dirac type spectrum with a pair of Weyl nodes. We observe that a tilt along the quadratic direction can give rise to an energy imbalanc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055406] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the electronic band structure and optical conductivity of a two-dimensional anisotropic semimetal with tilted semi-Dirac spectrum and imbalanced Weyl nodes.
motivation: To understand how tilt-induced energy imbalance between Weyl nodes affects the optical properties of 2D anisotropic semimetals.
method: Theoretical calculation of electronic band structure and optical conductivity using a tilted semi-Dirac model.
result: The tilt along the quadratic direction creates an energy imbalance between Weyl nodes, leading to distinct features in optical conductivity.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the optical response of 2D anisotropic semimetals with imbalanced Weyl nodes.

title: Topological Edge States In Two-dimensional ${\mathbb{Z}}_{4}$ Potts Paramagnet Protected By The ${\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{×3}$ Symmetry
authors: Hrant Topchyan, Tigran Hakobyan, Mkhitar Mirumyan, Tigran A. Sedrakyan, And Ara Sedrakyan
abstract:
Author(s): Hrant Topchyan, Tigran Hakobyan, Mkhitar Mirumyan, Tigran A. Sedrakyan, and Ara Sedrakyan

We construct a two-dimensional bosonic symmetry-protected topological (SPT) paramagnet protected by an on-site [MATH] symmetry, starting from a three-component [MATH] Potts paramagnet on a triangular lattice. Within the group-cohomology framework, ${H}^{3}[G,U(1)]≅{\ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065111] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs a two-dimensional bosonic symmetry-protected topological (SPT) paramagnet protected by Z4^×3 symmetry using group cohomology.
motivation: To extend the understanding of SPT phases in bosonic systems with discrete symmetries beyond the well-studied Z2 case.
method: Starting from a three-component Z4 Potts paramagnet on a triangular lattice, the authors apply group-cohomology framework to construct the SPT state.
result: They identify topological edge states characteristic of the SPT phase protected by the Z4^×3 symmetry.
conclusion: The work provides a concrete example of a bosonic SPT phase with Z4^×3 symmetry, contributing to the classification of topological phases.

title: Strongly Correlated Model Of Acousticlike Plasmons Persisting Across The Phase Diagram Of Cuprate Superconductors
authors: Luciano Zinni, Hiroyuki Yamase, Matthias Hepting, Matías Bejas, And Andrés Greco
abstract:
Author(s): Luciano Zinni, Hiroyuki Yamase, Matthias Hepting, Matías Bejas, and Andrés Greco

Layered two-dimensional electron systems exhibit both optical and acousticlike plasmons around the Brillouin-zone center. In the layered cuprate [MATH], resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) has detected corresponding acousticlike plasmons in a …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051103] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies acousticlike plasmons in cuprate superconductors using a strongly correlated model and RIXS.
motivation: To understand the nature of acousticlike plasmons in layered cuprates and their persistence across the phase diagram.
method: The authors employ a strongly correlated model and compare with resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) data.
result: Acousticlike plasmons are found to persist across the phase diagram of cuprate superconductors.
conclusion: The work provides insight into collective excitations in cuprates but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Enhancement And Reentrant Topological Transitions In A Mosaic Trimer Lattice
authors: Xiatao Wang, Li Wang, And Shu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xiatao Wang, Li Wang, and Shu Chen

We study the topological properties of a one-dimensional quasiperiodic-potential-modulated mosaic trimer lattice. To begin with, we first investigate the topological properties of the model in the clean limit free of quasiperiodic modulation based on analytical derivations and numerical calculations…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014204] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phases in a one-dimensional quasiperiodic mosaic trimer lattice, focusing on topological enhancement and reentrant transitions.
motivation: To understand topological properties in quasiperiodic systems and explore novel topological transitions beyond conventional periodic lattices.
method: Analytical derivations and numerical calculations are used to characterize the topological invariants and phase diagram of the mosaic trimer lattice with quasiperiodic modulation.
result: The system exhibits topological enhancement and reentrant topological transitions as a function of the quasiperiodic potential strength.
conclusion: The findings reveal rich topological behavior in quasiperiodic systems, contributing to the understanding of topological phases in disordered lattices.

title: Long-range Spin Glass In A Field At Zero Temperature
authors: Maria Chiara Angelini, Saverio Palazzi, Giorgio Parisi, And Tommaso Rizzo
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Chiara Angelini, Saverio Palazzi, Giorgio Parisi, and Tommaso Rizzo

We compute the critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field on a one-dimensional long-range model, a proxy for higher-dimensional systems. Our approach is based on a novel loop expansion within the Bethe [MATH]-layer formalism, whose adaptation to this specific case is de…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014410] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field using a long-range one-dimensional model and a novel loop expansion within the Bethe-layer formalism.
motivation: Understanding spin glass transitions in a field is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics, and the long-range model serves as a proxy for higher-dimensional systems.
method: The authors develop a loop expansion within the Bethe-layer formalism adapted to the long-range spin glass model to compute critical exponents at zero temperature.
result: They obtain the critical exponents for the zero-temperature transition in a field, providing insights into the behavior of spin glasses.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of spin glasses but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics as defined in the research interests.

title: Real-time Detection Of Critical Slowing Down In Ultrafast Quenches Of Superconductivity
authors: Guillermo Nava Antonio, Théo Courtois, Corentin Pfaff, KM Shivangi Shukla, Asle Sudbø, Stéphane Mangin, Thomas Hauet, And Chiara Ciccarelli
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Nava Antonio, Théo Courtois, Corentin Pfaff, KM Shivangi Shukla, Asle Sudbø, Stéphane Mangin, Thomas Hauet, and Chiara Ciccarelli

We employ optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy to chart the ultrafast superconductivity suppression in NbN over a broad range of excitation fluences. Our measurements uncover a pronounced lengthening of the superconductivity quenching time when the absorbed optical energy is close to the condensation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014505] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies ultrafast suppression of superconductivity in NbN using optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy, focusing on critical slowing down near the condensation energy threshold.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of superconductivity suppression under ultrafast optical excitation is important for fundamental physics and potential applications in ultrafast electronics.
method: Optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy is used to measure the superconductivity quenching time as a function of absorbed optical energy in NbN thin films.
result: A pronounced lengthening of the quenching time is observed when the absorbed energy approaches the condensation energy, indicating critical slowing down.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the non-equilibrium dynamics of superconductors and the nature of the phase transition under ultrafast excitation.

title: Majorana Signatures In Planar Tunneling Through A Kitaev Spin Liquid
authors: Weiyao Li, Vitor Dantas, Wen-Han Kao, And Natalia B. Perkins
abstract:
Author(s): Weiyao Li, Vitor Dantas, Wen-Han Kao, and Natalia B. Perkins

We propose a planar tunneling setup to probe vacancy-bound Majorana modes in the chiral Kitaev spin liquid. In this geometry, the inelastic tunneling conductance can be expressed directly in terms of real-space spin correlations, establishing a link between measurable spectra and the underlying frac…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024410] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Majorana signatures in planar tunneling through a Kitaev spin liquid, focusing on vacancy-bound Majorana modes and their detection via spin correlations.
motivation: To propose a tunneling setup that can probe Majorana modes in Kitaev spin liquids, which are of interest for topological quantum computation.
method: The authors model planar tunneling conductance in terms of real-space spin correlations and analyze the signatures of vacancy-bound Majorana modes.
result: They establish a direct link between inelastic tunneling conductance and spin correlations, enabling detection of Majorana modes.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a feasible experimental probe for Majorana physics in Kitaev spin liquids.

title: Revising The Superexchange Model For The Planar Iridate ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{2}{\mathrm{IrO}}_{4}$: From An Analytical Approach To $ab Initio$ Quantum-chemical Computations
authors: L. Siurakshina
abstract:
Author(s): L. Siurakshina

A modified spin-orbital superexchange theory is developed to derive the effective spin Hamiltonian [MATH] governing the exchange interactions between pseudospins-[MATH] on a square lattice, as occurs, for instance, in planar iridium oxide [MATH]. The proced…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024412] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a modified spin-orbital superexchange theory to derive an effective spin Hamiltonian for the planar iridate Ba2IrO4.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of Ba2IrO4, a material with strong spin-orbit coupling, by deriving an accurate effective spin model.
method: The authors use an analytical approach combined with ab initio quantum-chemical computations to derive a spin-orbital superexchange model.
result: A modified superexchange theory is presented that yields an effective spin Hamiltonian for pseudospin-1/2 on a square lattice.
conclusion: The derived model provides a better description of the exchange interactions in Ba2IrO4, improving upon previous models.

title: Interaction-driven Quantum Criticality In Two-dimensional Quadratic Band Crossing Semimetals With Time-reversal Symmetry Breaking
authors: Yi-Kun Fang And Jing Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Kun Fang and Jing Wang

We present a systematic investigation of all 16 marginally relevant fermion-fermion interactions in two-dimensional (2D) time-reversal symmetry-breaking kagome semimetals hosting a quadratic band crossing point (QBCP). Employing a momentum-shell renormalization-group approach that treats every inter…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034102] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven quantum criticality in 2D time-reversal symmetry-breaking kagome semimetals with a quadratic band crossing point.
motivation: To understand the effects of fermion-fermion interactions in quadratic band crossing semimetals, which are relevant to condensed matter physics.
method: A momentum-shell renormalization-group approach is used to analyze all 16 marginally relevant interactions.
result: The analysis reveals the phase diagram and critical behavior of the system under various interaction strengths.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic classification of interaction-driven quantum critical points in this class of materials.

title: Higher-order Topological type-II Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: Liren Chen, Jinglin Liu, Jingming Chen, Bolun Huang, And Zhen Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Liren Chen, Jinglin Liu, Jingming Chen, Bolun Huang, and Zhen Gao

Recently, higher-order topological phases have been extended from Euclidean lattices to non-Euclidean hyperbolic lattices. Though higher-order topological type-I hyperbolic lattices have been extensively studied, their counterpart, higher-order topological type-II hyperbolic lattices, have never yet…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034107] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order topological phases in hyperbolic lattices, extending type-II topological insulators to non-Euclidean geometry.
motivation: Higher-order topological phases have been studied in Euclidean lattices and recently extended to hyperbolic lattices for type-I, but type-II hyperbolic lattices remain unexplored.
method: The authors construct a hyperbolic lattice model and analyze its topological properties using band theory and corner state calculations.
result: They demonstrate the existence of higher-order topological type-II phases in hyperbolic lattices, characterized by protected corner states.
conclusion: This work expands the understanding of topological phases in non-Euclidean geometries, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Observing Complementary Lucas Sequences Using non-Hermitian Zero Modes
authors: Li Ge
abstract:
Author(s): Li Ge

The Lucas sequences are integers defined by a homogeneous recurrence relation. They include the well-known Fibonacci numbers, which appear abundantly in nature. The complementary Lucas numbers, defined by the same recurrence relation, are less well-known. In this work, we show that such complementar…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034108] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that complementary Lucas sequences can be observed using non-Hermitian zero modes in a photonic system.
motivation: Lucas sequences, including Fibonacci numbers, appear in nature, but complementary Lucas numbers are less known; the authors aim to demonstrate their physical observability.
method: The authors use a non-Hermitian photonic system with zero modes to map the recurrence relation of complementary Lucas sequences onto physical observables.
result: They show that the complementary Lucas numbers can be extracted from the system's response, providing a physical realization of these mathematical sequences.
conclusion: This work bridges number theory and non-Hermitian physics, offering a new platform to study integer sequences experimentally.

title: Percolation And Criticality Of Systems With Competing Interactions On Bethe Lattices: Limitations And Potential Strengths Of Cluster Schemes
authors: Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, And Marco Tarzia
abstract:
Author(s): Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, and Marco Tarzia

Cluster-based algorithms have led to remarkably efficient Monte Carlo sampling schemes that reduce critical slowing down. The authors demonstrate that seeking such cluster schemes for frustrated systems is futile, but they leave open the possibility that alternate approaches could be devised.

#TechnicalAdvancement #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014114] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies percolation and criticality in frustrated systems on Bethe lattices, showing that cluster algorithms fail to reduce critical slowing down.
motivation: Cluster algorithms are efficient for non-frustrated systems, but their applicability to frustrated systems is unclear. The authors aim to test whether such schemes can work for systems with competing interactions.
method: The authors analyze cluster-based Monte Carlo schemes on Bethe lattices with competing interactions, using theoretical arguments and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that cluster algorithms do not reduce critical slowing down for frustrated systems, but suggest that alternative approaches might still be possible.
conclusion: Seeking cluster schemes for frustrated systems is futile, but the possibility of alternate approaches remains open.

title: Stability Of Delay-coupled Reaction-diffusion Systems With Turing Or Wave Instability
authors: Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, And Naoyuki Hara
abstract:
Author(s): Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, and Naoyuki Hara

A quenching phenomenon that emerges in coupled oscillators, namely, amplitude death (AD), has been widely accepted. The present paper analytically deals with AD in two identical reaction-diffusion systems with periodic boundary or zero-flux boundary conditions that are coupled by a diffusive connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014207] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies amplitude death in delay-coupled reaction-diffusion systems with Turing or wave instability.
motivation: Understanding amplitude death in coupled oscillators is important for controlling oscillations in biological and chemical systems.
method: The authors analytically investigate two identical reaction-diffusion systems coupled by diffusive connections under periodic or zero-flux boundary conditions.
result: They derive conditions for amplitude death and analyze the role of delay and coupling strength.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into quenching phenomena in spatially extended systems with time delays.

title: From Active To Odd To Smart Matter
authors: Olivier Dauchot
abstract:
Author(s): Olivier Dauchot

Active matter taught us that microscopic energy injection can lead to macroscopic dynamical order. Odd elasticity revealed that active solids can turn deformation into work. The next question is sharper: can matter learn what it is good for?


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 011001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the evolution from active matter to odd elasticity and poses the question of whether matter can learn, but does not present technical results in quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The author aims to outline a research direction where active matter systems might exhibit learning capabilities, building on concepts of odd elasticity.
method: The paper is a perspective or commentary, not a technical research article; it does not present a specific method.
result: No concrete results are presented; the paper is forward-looking and conceptual.
conclusion: The paper suggests that the next frontier is to explore if matter can learn, but does not provide evidence or a framework.

title: Interaction Of Solitons With Saturable Gain
authors: Akhilesh K. S. And Omri Gat
abstract:
Author(s): Akhilesh K. S. and Omri Gat

We study the tail-overlap interaction of a well-separated pair of dissipative solitons in systems with slow saturable gain. Gain saturation introduces nonlocal terms in the soliton field equation that depend on the total energy and therefore invalidate the standard methods used to study overlap inte…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014205] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interaction of dissipative solitons in systems with slow saturable gain, focusing on tail-overlap effects.
motivation: Understanding soliton interactions is important for nonlinear optics and laser physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating nonlocal gain saturation terms and analyze the interaction dynamics of well-separated soliton pairs.
result: They find that gain saturation introduces nonlocal effects that modify the standard soliton interaction picture.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of dissipative solitons but has no relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Eigenvector Localization And Universal Regime Transitions In Multiplex Networks: A Perturbative Approach
authors: Joan Hernàndez Tey And Emanuele Cozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Joan Hernàndez Tey and Emanuele Cozzo

We study the transition between layer-localized and delocalized regimes in a general contact-based contagion model on multiplex networks. Using the inverse participation ratio, we characterize how activity shifts from being confined to a single layer to spreading across the entire system. Through a …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014307] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies eigenvector localization and regime transitions in multiplex networks using a perturbative approach, applied to a contagion model.
motivation: Understanding how activity localizes in multiplex networks is important for modeling spreading processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use the inverse participation ratio and perturbation theory to analyze the transition between layer-localized and delocalized regimes in multiplex networks.
result: They characterize the conditions under which activity shifts from being confined to a single layer to spreading across the entire multiplex system.
conclusion: The work provides insights into multiplex network dynamics but is not relevant to the specified research interests.

title: Mechanical Waveform Memory In An Athermal Random Medium
authors: Eamon Dwight And D. Candela
abstract:
Author(s): Eamon Dwight and D. Candela

This manuscript investigates static waveform memory in a system of jammed, soft, frictional particles. It is shown that a small, time-dependent shear strain applied during progressive compression can imprint an arbitrary waveform, which is recalled in time-reversed order upon decompression. The conditions that allow memory formation and the limits of memory readout are established.

#TimelyTopic #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015406] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mechanical waveform memory in a jammed granular system, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding memory effects in athermal disordered systems is of fundamental interest in soft matter physics.
method: The authors apply a time-dependent shear strain during compression of soft frictional particles and measure the recalled waveform upon decompression.
result: They demonstrate that arbitrary waveforms can be imprinted and recalled in time-reversed order, and characterize the conditions and limits of this memory.
conclusion: The work provides insights into memory formation in athermal systems but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spatiotemporal Activity-driven Networks
authors: Zsófia Simon And Jari Saramäki
abstract:
Author(s): Zsófia Simon and Jari Saramäki

Temporal-network models have provided key insights into how time-varying connectivity shapes dynamical processes such as spreading. Among them, the activity-driven model is a widely used, analytically tractable benchmark. Yet many temporal networks, such as those of physical proximity, are also embe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014306] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the activity-driven temporal network model to incorporate spatiotemporal constraints, analyzing how spatial embedding affects spreading dynamics.
motivation: Temporal networks often ignore spatial constraints, yet many real-world networks (e.g., physical proximity) are embedded in space. The authors aim to develop a tractable model that captures both temporal and spatial aspects.
method: The authors introduce a spatiotemporal activity-driven model where nodes move in a continuous space and interact when within a certain distance, with activity rates governing interaction initiation. They derive analytical expressions for the epidemic threshold and spreading speed.
result: The model reveals that spatial constraints can significantly alter spreading dynamics compared to purely temporal models, with a critical spatial scale that separates fast and slow spreading regimes.
conclusion: Spatiotemporal activity-driven networks provide a more realistic framework for modeling spreading processes in systems where both time and space matter, such as human mobility and disease spread.

title: Neural Optimization Of The Most Probable Paths Of Three-dimensional Active Brownian Particles
authors: Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Changhao Li, Zhanglin Hou, Ziluo Zhang, Xinpeng Xu, Li-Shing Lin, Kenta Ishimoto, Kento Yasuda, And Shigeyuki Komura
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Changhao Li, Zhanglin Hou, Ziluo Zhang, Xinpeng Xu, Li-Shing Lin, Kenta Ishimoto, Kento Yasuda, and Shigeyuki Komura

By minimizing the Onsager-Machlup integral with a neural-network framework, this Letter determines the most probable paths of a three-dimensional active Brownian particle. These optimal transition pathways exhibit distinct geometric shifts from planar to helical shapes. The work provides a versatile framework for exploring optimal transition pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems.

#WellStructured #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012103] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a neural-network framework to find optimal transition paths of active Brownian particles in three dimensions.
motivation: Understanding the most probable paths in active matter systems is important for predicting their dynamics, but analytical solutions are often intractable.
method: The authors minimize the Onsager-Machlup integral using a neural-network approach to compute optimal transition pathways for a three-dimensional active Brownian particle.
result: The optimal paths exhibit distinct geometric shifts from planar to helical shapes depending on parameters.
conclusion: The neural-network framework provides a versatile tool for exploring optimal transition pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems.

title: Can Machine Learning Truly Decode Phase Transitions? A Deep Dive Into The Ising Model With Competing Interactions
authors: Maninder Kaur, Ying Wai Li, Dilina Perera, And David P. Landau
abstract:
Author(s): Maninder Kaur, Ying Wai Li, Dilina Perera, and David P. Landau

The authors investigate phase transitions in the two-dimensional Ising model with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions, by combining machine learning with simulations and finite-size scaling. The results show that machine learning can decode ordering patterns, extract order-parameter analogs, and reproduce critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.

#MachineLearningSpotlight #TimelyTopic


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014104] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to study phase transitions in the 2D Ising model with competing interactions, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore whether machine learning can decode ordering patterns and critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.
method: Combines machine learning with Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling to analyze the 2D Ising model with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions.
result: Machine learning can extract order-parameter analogs and reproduce critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.
conclusion: Machine learning is a useful tool for studying phase transitions in classical spin systems, but the work is purely classical and not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tunable Bands In One-dimensional Fractional Quantum Media
authors: Brenden R. Guyette, Joshua M. Lewis, And Lincoln D. Carr
abstract:
Author(s): Brenden R. Guyette, Joshua M. Lewis, and Lincoln D. Carr

Fractional calculus has become an essential framework in geophysics, optics, and biological systems to capture long-range correlations and anomalous transport. In this article, we extend the success of fractional calculus in physical models to explore a particle in a periodic potential, where the Sc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014106] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a particle in a periodic potential using fractional calculus, focusing on tunable band structures in one-dimensional fractional quantum media.
motivation: Fractional calculus captures long-range correlations and anomalous transport in various physical systems; extending it to periodic potentials may reveal novel band properties.
method: The authors apply fractional calculus to the Schrödinger equation with a periodic potential, solving for energy bands as a function of the fractional derivative order.
result: They find that the fractional order tunes the band structure, including band gaps and dispersion relations, in ways not present in standard quantum mechanics.
conclusion: Fractional quantum mechanics offers a new degree of freedom for engineering band structures, with potential applications in condensed matter and photonics.

title: Effects Of Quenched Disorder In Three-dimensional Lattice ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Gauge Higgs Models
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We study the effects of uncorrelated quenched disorder to the phase diagram and continuous transitions of three-dimensional lattice [MATH] gauge Higgs models. For this purpose, we consider two types of quenched disorder, associated with the sites and plaquettes of the cubic lattice. In b…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014107] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effects of quenched disorder on phase transitions in three-dimensional lattice Z2 gauge Higgs models.
motivation: Understanding how disorder affects phase diagrams and critical behavior in gauge theories is important for condensed matter and high-energy physics.
method: The authors consider two types of quenched disorder (site and plaquette) and use Monte Carlo simulations to analyze the phase diagram and critical exponents.
result: Quenched disorder modifies the phase diagram and can change the order of phase transitions, with some transitions becoming first-order or suppressed.
conclusion: Disorder has significant effects on the critical properties of gauge Higgs models, which may have implications for understanding disordered systems in quantum field theory.

title: Field-controlled Interfacial Transport And Pinning In An Active Spin System
authors: Mintu Karmakar, Matthieu Mangeat, Swarnajit Chatterjee, Heiko Rieger, And Raja Paul
abstract:
Author(s): Mintu Karmakar, Matthieu Mangeat, Swarnajit Chatterjee, Heiko Rieger, and Raja Paul

Field control provides a practical route to programmable active matter, yet how weak fields modify nonequilibrium coexistence and interfaces remains unclear. To address this, we study a minimal flocking model of active Potts particles coupled to an external field and show that even weak fields can r…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014108] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies field-controlled interfacial transport and pinning in an active spin system, focusing on flocking models and nonequilibrium coexistence.
motivation: To understand how weak external fields modify nonequilibrium coexistence and interfaces in active matter systems.
method: A minimal flocking model of active Potts particles coupled to an external field is studied, likely via simulations.
result: Even weak fields can significantly alter interfacial transport and pinning behavior.
conclusion: Field control provides a practical route to programmable active matter, but the work is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Complete Local Expansion Of The Availability Function In Random Sequential Adsorption Of Aligned Squares At Low Density: Termination At Fourth Order
authors: F. Ţolea And M. Ţolea
abstract:
Author(s): F. Ţolea and M. Ţolea

We consider random sequential adsorption (RSA) of aligned squares and derive the low-coverage expansion of the availability function [MATH], the fraction of positions accessible to an additional square, up to fourth order in the coverage [MATH]. At low coverage, the reduction of available space can be …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014110] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies random sequential adsorption of aligned squares, deriving a low-coverage expansion of the availability function up to fourth order.
motivation: Understanding the kinetics of irreversible deposition processes is important for modeling physical phenomena such as protein adsorption or particle deposition.
method: The authors perform a systematic low-density expansion of the availability function for RSA of aligned squares, computing contributions up to fourth order in coverage using combinatorial and geometric arguments.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the availability function up to fourth order, showing how the available area decreases with coverage.
conclusion: The results provide a more accurate description of the RSA process at low densities, but the work is purely classical and statistical mechanical, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Persistent Imbalance In Open Networks With Coevolutionary Dynamics
authors: S. Arab Mohammadi, H. Jafari, A. Kargaran, A. Hosseiny, And G. Reza Jafari
abstract:
Author(s): S. Arab Mohammadi, H. Jafari, A. Kargaran, A. Hosseiny, and G. Reza Jafari

Societies are quintessential open systems, shaped by internal dynamics as well as external influences. The question is how these external influences alter the collective behavior and network dynamics. To answer this, we investigate coevolutionary balance dynamics in a system of independent and open …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014301] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coevolutionary balance dynamics in open social networks, focusing on persistent imbalance under external influences.
motivation: Understanding how external influences alter collective behavior and network dynamics in open systems.
method: Investigates coevolutionary dynamics in a system of independent and open networks using a balance theory framework.
result: Identifies conditions for persistent imbalance in open networks with coevolutionary dynamics.
conclusion: External influences can sustain imbalance in social networks, which has implications for understanding societal dynamics.

title: Ising Phase Transitions In Networks With Tunable Degree-degree Correlations
authors: R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We present a systematic numerical study of the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations. The networks are constructed with a truncated power-law degree distribution, ensuring finite moments, and correlations are introduced via the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rew…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations, focusing on phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding how degree-degree correlations affect phase transitions in complex networks is important for statistical physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors construct networks with truncated power-law degree distributions and introduce correlations via the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rewiring method, then perform Monte Carlo simulations of the Ising model.
result: They find that degree-degree correlations significantly shift the critical temperature and alter the universality class of the phase transition.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the role of network topology in phase transitions, but has no direct relevance to quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.

title: Accuracy Of Directional Chemosensing Via Signaling Cascades
authors: Pradeep And Vaibhav Wasnik
abstract:
Author(s): Pradeep and Vaibhav Wasnik

Cells interpret noisy biochemical signals with remarkable precision, raising fundamental questions about the limits of sensing. While receptor-level constraints in chemosensing are well characterized, the role of intracellular signaling remains underexplored. We develop a theoretical framework combi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for directional chemosensing via signaling cascades, focusing on accuracy limits in biochemical sensing.
motivation: To understand how cells achieve precise chemosensing despite noise, and to quantify the role of intracellular signaling cascades beyond receptor-level constraints.
method: A theoretical framework combining information theory and statistical physics to model signal propagation through a cascade of biochemical reactions.
result: The framework reveals fundamental limits on directional sensing accuracy imposed by the signaling cascade, showing trade-offs between sensitivity and noise.
conclusion: Intracellular signaling cascades significantly impact chemosensing accuracy, and the derived limits can guide understanding of cellular information processing.

title: Supercritical Transition Of Yukawa Fluids Identified By Excess Entropy
authors: Ao Xu And Yan Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Xu and Yan Feng

Equilibrium molecular dynamical simulations of three-dimensional (3D) Yukawa fluids are performed to investigate thermodynamics and supercritical transition of 3D dusty plasma fluids. The normalized reduced excess entropy [MATH] of 3D Yukawa fluids (where …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015203] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the supercritical transition of Yukawa fluids using excess entropy, a topic in classical statistical mechanics of dusty plasmas.
motivation: Understanding the supercritical state of matter is important for applications like dusty plasmas, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of 3D Yukawa fluids are performed to compute the normalized reduced excess entropy.
result: The excess entropy is used to identify a supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic characterization of supercritical Yukawa fluids, but lacks relevance to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: From Geometry To Strategy: Symmetry Breaking In Cooperative Multiagent Active Dynamics
authors: Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, And Sergey Savel'ev
abstract:
Author(s): Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, and Sergey Savel'ev

We investigate the emergence of cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems, where autonomous agents, modeled as active particles, learn to capture targets dynamically regenerated in geometrically distinct arenas. Using proximal policy optimization, we study ci…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems using active particles, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how autonomous agents learn to cooperate or compete in dynamic environments with geometric constraints.
method: Uses proximal policy optimization to train agents modeled as active particles in arenas with regenerating targets.
result: Agents exhibit symmetry-breaking transitions between cooperative and competitive strategies depending on arena geometry.
conclusion: Geometry can induce emergent strategic behaviors in multiagent active systems, relevant to collective robotics and active matter.

title: Active Deformation Enhances Target Scanning In Crowded Two-dimensional Self-propelled Particle Simulations
authors: Lucas E. Wiebke And Daniel R. Parisi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas E. Wiebke and Daniel R. Parisi

Self-propelled particles (SPPs) model diverse transport phenomena, including T-cell motility within crowded lymph nodes. Efficient scanning of antigen-presenting cells (APCs) by T cells remains poorly understood under dense conditions. Here we simulate a two-dimensional system of radius-oscillating …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active deformation in self-propelled particles to enhance target scanning in crowded environments, motivated by T-cell motility.
motivation: Efficient scanning of antigen-presenting cells by T cells in dense lymph nodes is poorly understood; active deformation may improve search efficiency.
method: Simulations of a two-dimensional system of radius-oscillating self-propelled particles are performed to model T-cell behavior.
result: Active deformation enhances target scanning efficiency in crowded conditions compared to non-deforming particles.
conclusion: Active deformation is a beneficial strategy for improving search in dense environments, with implications for biological transport.

title: Nonclassical Interfacial Response In Ionic Liquids At Blocking Electrodes
authors: Mahdi Yavarian And Roderick Melnik
abstract:
Author(s): Mahdi Yavarian and Roderick Melnik

The linear response of a symmetric binary ionic liquid confined between two parallel, blocking electrodes is analyzed under the influence of electrostatic correlations [MATH] while systematically comparing the effects of two distinct interfacial boundary conditions: the Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev (B…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015502] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the linear response of ionic liquids between blocking electrodes, focusing on electrostatic correlations and boundary conditions.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of ionic liquids at interfaces is important for applications like supercapacitors and batteries.
method: The authors analyze a symmetric binary ionic liquid model using linear response theory and compare two interfacial boundary conditions (Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev and others).
result: They find nonclassical interfacial responses due to electrostatic correlations, with significant differences depending on the boundary condition.
conclusion: The choice of boundary condition critically affects the predicted response, highlighting the need for accurate modeling in electrochemical systems.

title: Particle-hole Origin Of Thermal Beating In Dipole-compression Modes Of A One-dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, And Giulia de Rosi
abstract:
Author(s): Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, and Giulia De Rosi

This work reports a beating signal of two dipole-compression collective mode frequencies evolving from the low-temperature phononic hydrodynamic regime to the collisionless limit at the hole-induced anomaly temperature. The lower (higher) frequency originates from hole (particle) spectral states, and the temperature dependence of their relative excitation strengths reflects the thermal population imbalance between particle and hole states across the anomaly temperature.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032003] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal beating in dipole-compression modes of a 1D Bose gas, attributing it to particle-hole spectral states.
motivation: Understanding collective mode behavior in ultracold gases across temperature regimes is important for many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze the temperature dependence of two dipole-compression mode frequencies using a particle-hole picture.
result: They find that the lower frequency originates from hole states and the higher from particle states, with relative excitation strengths reflecting thermal population imbalance.
conclusion: The beating signal arises from the interplay of particle and hole excitations, providing insight into the crossover from hydrodynamic to collisionless regimes.

title: Physics-informed Neural Networks For Solving Saddle-point Equations In Strong-field Physics With Tailored Fields
authors: Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, And Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, and Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria

We develop an unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) to solve the saddle-point equations (SPEs) governing direct above-threshold ionization (ATI) within the strong-field approximation. This setting provides a well-understood test bed in which the saddle-point structure is known for tail…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033029] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to solve saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, specifically for above-threshold ionization.
motivation: To develop a machine learning approach for efficiently solving saddle-point equations that arise in strong-field physics, which are computationally intensive with traditional methods.
method: An unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) is designed to solve the saddle-point equations governing direct above-threshold ionization within the strong-field approximation.
result: The PINN successfully reproduces known saddle-point structures and provides accurate solutions for tailored fields, demonstrating the feasibility of neural networks for such problems.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a promising alternative for solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, potentially extending to more complex scenarios.

title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo Sampling To Model Lagrangian Tracer Dispersion In Turbulent Boundary Layer
authors: Fabian Schindler And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Schindler and Jörg Schumacher

We present a quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QE-MCMC) method to sample turbulent acceleration vectors from a joint target distribution that depends on all three components and height to model the transport and dispersion of massless Lagrangian tracer particles in two different turbulent s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033031] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo to model Lagrangian tracer dispersion in turbulent boundary layers, a computational fluid dynamics problem.
motivation: To improve sampling efficiency for turbulent acceleration vectors in Lagrangian particle dispersion models using quantum computing.
method: A quantum-enhanced MCMC algorithm is developed to sample from a joint target distribution of turbulent acceleration components and height.
result: The QE-MCMC method demonstrates improved sampling efficiency compared to classical MCMC for the turbulent flow scenarios considered.
conclusion: Quantum-enhanced sampling can benefit computational fluid dynamics, but the paper focuses on application rather than fundamental quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Daoning Wu and Jie Lin

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation in confined spaces, relevant to biophysics and soft matter, but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates often form near surfaces, but the effect of confinement on phase separation is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze phase separation near a surface under finite molecule number constraints.
result: They find that surface phase separation is significantly altered by confinement, with implications for cellular organization.
conclusion: Surface effects and finite size are crucial for understanding phase separation in biological cells.

title: Noiseless Limit And Improved-prior Limit Of The Maximum Entropy Method And Their Implications For The Analytic Continuation Problem
authors: Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, And Tobias Dornheim
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, and Tobias Dornheim

Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are uniquely capable of providing exact simulations of quantum many-body systems. Unfortunately, the applications of a QMC simulation are limited because extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem. Across the many fields that us…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033009] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the maximum entropy method for analytic continuation in quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on its noiseless and improved-prior limits.
motivation: Quantum Monte Carlo methods provide exact simulations of quantum many-body systems but extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem, which is ill-posed.
method: The authors study the maximum entropy method in the noiseless limit and with improved priors, deriving theoretical bounds and demonstrating their implications for the analytic continuation problem.
result: They show that in the noiseless limit, the maximum entropy method can recover exact spectral functions, and improved priors can significantly enhance reconstruction accuracy.
conclusion: The findings provide guidance for choosing priors and noise levels in practical analytic continuation, improving the reliability of dynamic property extraction from QMC data.

title: Markov Inequality As A Tool For Linear-scaling Estimation Of Local Observables
authors: H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:
Author(s): H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, and J. M. Viana Parente Lopes

We introduce a linear-scaling stochastic method to compute real-space maps of any positive local spectral operator in a tight-binding model. By employing positive semidefinite estimators, the sampling error at each site can be rigorously bounded relative to the mean via the Markov inequality, overco…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033015] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A linear-scaling stochastic method for computing local spectral operators in tight-binding models using Markov inequality to bound sampling error.
motivation: To efficiently compute real-space maps of local observables in large tight-binding models without full diagonalization.
method: Uses positive semidefinite estimators and Markov inequality to bound sampling error per site, achieving linear scaling with system size.
result: The method provides rigorous error bounds and linear-scaling computational cost for local spectral operators.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient and reliable computation of local observables in large quantum systems, with potential applications in condensed matter physics.

title: Structural And Thermal Confinement Of Schwarz Crystals
authors: Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, And Ke Lu

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033017] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the structural and thermal confinement of Schwarz crystals, a type of nanostructured solid with triply periodic minimal surface grain boundaries.
motivation: To understand how structural units interact and how thermal transport occurs in Schwarz crystals, which exhibit exceptional thermal and mechanical stability.
method: The authors likely use experimental techniques such as neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to investigate the structural and thermal properties.
result: The paper reveals insights into the thermal confinement and structural stability of Schwarz crystals.
conclusion: Schwarz crystals have unique thermal and mechanical properties due to their nanograin structure and TPMS boundaries, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Arbitrary Control Of non-Hermitian Skin Modes Via Disorder And An Electric Field
authors: Zhao-Fan Cai, Yang Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Xiaomin Wei, Zhongmin Yang, Tao Liu, And Franco Nori

However, in higher dimensions, achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate remains a major challenge. Here…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033021] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the control of non-Hermitian skin modes using disorder and electric fields in higher dimensions.
motivation: Achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate in higher-dimensional non-Hermitian systems is a major challenge.
method: The authors propose using disorder and electric fields to arbitrarily control the localization of non-Hermitian skin modes.
result: They demonstrate that by tuning disorder strength and electric field, skin modes can be directed to desired boundaries.
conclusion: This work provides a method for controlling non-Hermitian skin effects, which may have applications in wave manipulation.

title: Engineering Magnetotransport Through Hierarchical Symmetry In Weyl Semimetal Superlattices
authors: Nathan C. Drucker, Federico Balduini, Jules Schadt, Lorenzo Rocchino, Tathagata Paul, Vicky Hasse, Claudia Felser, Heinz Schmid, Cezar B. Zota, And Bernd Gotsmann

Superlattice engineering, the introduction of periodic potentials to a material, can induce selective scattering events that modify the electrical properties of the material in predictable ways. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033023] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetotransport in Weyl semimetal superlattices, focusing on symmetry-induced electronic properties.
motivation: To explore how periodic potentials in 3D materials can engineer electrical properties via selective scattering.
method: The authors fabricate Weyl semimetal superlattices and measure magnetotransport, analyzing the role of hierarchical symmetry.
result: They demonstrate tunable magnetotransport behavior linked to the superlattice symmetry.
conclusion: Superlattice engineering in 3D semimetals offers a new route to control electronic transport.

title: Adversarial Vulnerability Of Machine-learning Surrogates For Computational Fluid Dynamics
authors: Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, And Jun-Jie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, and Jun-Jie Zhang

Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), yet their robustness to small, structured input perturbations remains insufficiently characterized. Conventional adversarial training is largely impractical for artificial intelligence for CFD (AI4CFD…

tldr: This paper studies adversarial vulnerability of machine-learning surrogates for computational fluid dynamics, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Machine-learning surrogates are used to accelerate CFD, but their robustness to small input perturbations is not well characterized.
method: The authors analyze adversarial attacks on neural network surrogates for CFD and evaluate their impact on prediction accuracy.
result: The surrogates are found to be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, which can cause significant errors in predicted flow fields.
conclusion: Adversarial robustness must be considered when deploying ML surrogates in CFD applications.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeet, M. Hörmann, and K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on a one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, showing accurate excitation energies.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical approach can efficiently compute quasiparticle excitations in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Extended Hot-electron Model And Current Bistability In Insulating $a\text{−}{\mathrm{Y}}_{x}{\mathrm{Si}}_{1\text{−}x}$ Films
authors: Le Hong Hoàng To, Andrés M. Somoza, Shamashis Sengupta, Louis Dumoulin, Laurent Bergé, Stefanos Marnieros, Claire Akiko Marrache-Kikuchi, And Miguel Ortuño

Electron-phonon interactions play a central role in determining charge and heat transport in condensed matter systems, but in disordered and low-dimensional materials, this coupling can be strongly suppressed, leading to nontrivial transport phenomena. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023360] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.

motivation: Understanding electron-phonon coupling in disordered materials is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend a hot-electron model to describe transport in amorphous YxSi1-x films and analyze current bistability.
result: They find that suppressed electron-phonon coupling leads to nontrivial transport phenomena including current bistability.
conclusion: The work contributes to condensed matter physics but is not relevant to the specified research interests.

title: Local Probe Evidence Supporting Altermagnetism In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{1/4}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: J. N. Graham, T. J. Hicken, Resham Babu Regmi, M. Janoschek, I. Mazin, H. Luetkens, N. J. Ghimire, And Z. Guguchia

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023361] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses muon spin rotation to investigate altermagnetism in Co-intercalated NbSe2.
motivation: To provide local probe evidence supporting the predicted altermagnetic state in Co1/4NbSe2, which has been suggested by neutron diffraction.
method: Muon spin rotation (μSR) measurements were performed on single crystals of Co1/4NbSe2 to probe the magnetic properties.
result: The μSR data provide evidence consistent with altermagnetism, supporting the predictions from neutron diffraction.
conclusion: The study confirms the altermagnetic nature of Co1/4NbSe2 using a local probe technique.

title: Composite Superconducting Orders And Magnetism In ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, And Carsten Timm
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, and Carsten Timm

Locally noncentrosymmetric materials are attracting significant attention due to the unique phenomena associated with sublattice degrees of freedom. The recently discovered heavy-fermion superconductor [MATH] has emerged as a compelling example of this class, garnerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023363] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies composite superconducting orders and magnetism in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeRh2As2, focusing on its locally noncentrosymmetric crystal structure.
motivation: CeRh2As2 exhibits unique superconducting properties due to its locally noncentrosymmetric structure, and understanding the interplay between superconductivity and magnetism is of fundamental interest.
method: The authors use a theoretical model based on a two-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian and solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations to study the superconducting and magnetic orders.
result: They find that the system can host composite superconducting orders, including a coexistence of spin-singlet and spin-triplet pairing, and that magnetic fluctuations play a key role.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the exotic superconducting phases in locally noncentrosymmetric materials, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Phase-space Methods For Near-resonant Light Propagation
authors: Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:

We study the dynamics of light interacting with a near-resonant atomic medium using the truncated Wigner and positive [MATH] phase-space representations. By mapping the atomic degrees of freedom via the Jordan-Schwinger transformation, we first analyze the system under unitary evolution before extendin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023353] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks phase-space methods for simulating near-resonant light propagation through atomic media.
motivation: To assess the accuracy and applicability of truncated Wigner and positive-P representations for modeling light-matter interactions beyond the perturbative regime.
method: Uses the Jordan-Schwinger transformation to map atomic degrees of freedom and compares the two phase-space methods under unitary and dissipative dynamics.
result: The positive-P method remains accurate for longer times than the truncated Wigner method, which fails due to negative Wigner functions.
conclusion: Phase-space methods can be effective for near-resonant propagation, but care is needed in choosing the representation based on the physical regime.

title: Correlated Many-body Quantum Dynamics Of The Peregrine Soliton
authors: D. Diplaris, G. A. Bougas, P. G. Kevrekidis, C.-L. Hung, P. Schmelcher, And S. I. Mistakidis
abstract:

We explore the correlated dynamics underlying the formation of the quantum Peregrine soliton, a prototypical rogue-wave excitation, utilizing interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in an ultracold bosonic gas confined in a one-dimensional box trap. The latter emulates the so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023355] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the correlated many-body quantum dynamics of the Peregrine soliton in an ultracold bosonic gas.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of rogue-wave excitations beyond mean-field theory.
method: Interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in a one-dimensional box trap, analyzed using exact diagonalization and time-dependent methods.
result: The correlated dynamics reveal deviations from mean-field predictions, including entanglement generation and fragmentation.
conclusion: Quantum correlations play a crucial role in the formation and dynamics of the Peregrine soliton.

title: Localization And Topological Signatures Under Periodic Twisting
authors: James Walkling, Antonio Štrkalj, And F. Nur Ünal
abstract:

We theoretically explore a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions formed by superimposing two square-lattice potentials. Motivated by the rich physics emerging at different twist angles between the two lattices at equilibrium, we introduce periodic twisting by continuous…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023356] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions with periodic twisting, revealing localization and topological signatures.
motivation: To explore the rich physics emerging from twist angles between two square lattices in a dynamical setting, extending equilibrium moiré systems.
method: The authors introduce periodic twisting by continuously varying the twist angle over time and analyze the resulting Floquet Hamiltonian using numerical simulations.
result: They observe localization phenomena and topological signatures, such as edge states and Chern numbers, that depend on the twisting protocol.
conclusion: Periodic twisting provides a new avenue to engineer topological and localized phases in driven systems.

title: Multipoles As Quantitative Order Parameters For Altermagnetic Spin Splitting
authors: Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, and Claude Ederer

We establish a quantitative relation between the altermagnetic spin splitting and different higher-order multipoles of the charge and magnetization density around the magnetic atoms. Magnetic multipoles such as octupoles or triakontadipoles have been suggested as potential ferroic order parameters f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023357] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a quantitative relation between altermagnetic spin splitting and higher-order multipoles of charge and magnetization density.
motivation: Altermagnetic spin splitting is a key phenomenon in condensed matter physics, and higher-order multipoles have been proposed as order parameters. A quantitative link was missing.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions and perform first-principles calculations to relate the spin splitting to magnetic octupoles and triakontadipoles.
result: They show that the magnitude of spin splitting is proportional to specific multipole moments, providing a quantitative order parameter.
conclusion: Higher-order magnetic multipoles serve as effective order parameters for altermagnetic spin splitting, enabling systematic material design.

title: Gapless Edge Gravitons And Quasiparticles In Fractional Quantum Hall Systems With Nonlocal Confinement
authors: Daniel Spasic-Mlacak And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Spasic-Mlacak and Nigel R. Cooper

Motivated by polaritonic platforms, this work investigates how nonlocal confinement affects the edge physics of fractional quantum Hall systems. It is found that the conventional edge modes are lost, to be replaced by new modes arising from bulk excitations—such as the graviton and quasielectron—that become gapless at the boundary.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022063] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies edge gravitons and quasiparticles in fractional quantum Hall systems with nonlocal confinement, motivated by polaritonic platforms.
motivation: To understand how nonlocal confinement affects edge physics in fractional quantum Hall systems, which is relevant for polaritonic platforms.
method: The authors theoretically investigate the edge modes of fractional quantum Hall systems under nonlocal confinement, analyzing the emergence of gapless modes from bulk excitations.
result: Conventional edge modes are lost and replaced by new gapless modes arising from bulk excitations such as the graviton and quasielectron.
conclusion: Nonlocal confinement fundamentally alters the edge physics of fractional quantum Hall systems, leading to novel gapless edge excitations.

title: Aging In A Two-dimensional Swarmalator Crystal With Delayed Interactions
authors: Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, And Oleg Kogan
abstract:

Time delay can have a significant impact on the properties of collective organization of active matter. In the previous paper [
tldr: This paper studies aging in a swarmalator crystal with delayed interactions, focusing on collective dynamics of active matter.
motivation: To understand how time delay affects the collective organization and aging behavior in a system of swarmalators, which are coupled oscillators with spatial interactions.
method: The authors analyze a two-dimensional swarmalator model with delayed interactions, using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis to study the emergence of aging and other dynamical phases.
result: They find that time delay can induce aging behavior in the swarmalator crystal, characterized by a gradual loss of order and synchronization.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques and optical antennas.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with tip-enhanced optical fluorescence, where the tip acts as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rapidly evolving field with potential for new physics and applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological electronic phases.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field theory.
method: The authors present a pedagogical review of field-theoretic methods for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, covering path integrals, Doi-Peliti formalism, and renormalization group techniques.
result: The review demonstrates how field-theoretic methods can be applied to a wide range of stochastic systems, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across multiple disciplines.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide crucial information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes recent observational constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of the dense matter equation of state.
