title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a platform for studying topological order and fractionalized excitations.
method: Review of theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental characterization of candidate materials (e.g., iridates, ruthenates).
result: Summarizes key properties such as chiral edge modes and the status of material candidates.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area with promising materials, but definitive experimental signatures are still sought.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, covering all facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an outlook on how these models can be incorporated into studies relevant to applications.
conclusion: The paper summarizes current theoretical approaches and suggests future directions for integrating them into applied research.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored. This review aims to bridge the gap between classical skyrmion physics and quantum phenomena.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmions, discussing quantum interactions underlying skyrmion formation and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights that skyrmions can exhibit quantum tunneling, superposition, and entanglement, and that their topological protection may be leveraged for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions offer a platform for exploring topological quantum phenomena and may have applications in quantum computing and spintronics, but further research is needed to realize practical quantum devices.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to test fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews a wide range of theoretical models and experimental techniques used to search for spin-dependent exotic interactions, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson-mediated interactions and highlights the most promising experimental approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions provide a rich avenue for probing new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further experimental and theoretical work is needed.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of circumstances where violations occur and identifies which assumptions are violated in each case.
result: It demonstrates that apparent violations arise from measurement conditions that do not satisfy the assumptions of the bounds, and that interesting material properties can be engineered.
conclusion: Classical thermodynamic bounds are not violated; rather, their assumptions must be carefully considered, and materials can be designed to circumvent these assumptions.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: The paper surveys various platforms (atomic, photonic, electronic) and techniques for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current capabilities and challenges in simulating exotic geometries with quantum systems.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential to bridge condensed matter, high-energy physics, and quantum simulation.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, exploring whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence and collapse, and experiments testing gravity-mediated entanglement between massive particles.
result: Ongoing experiments aim to determine whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement, guiding theoretical descriptions.
conclusion: Results from these experiments will inform the theoretical description of gravity on a laboratory scale.

title: When Vacuum Breaks: A Self-Consistency Test For Astrophysical Environments In Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals
authors: Lorenzo Copparoni, Rohit S. Chandramouli, And Enrico Barausse
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Copparoni, Rohit S. Chandramouli, and Enrico Barausse

Gravitational-wave signals are typically interpreted under the vacuum hypothesis, i.e., assuming negligible influence from the astrophysical environment. This assumption is expected to break down for low-frequency sources such as extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs), which are prime targets for the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021405] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests the vacuum hypothesis for gravitational wave signals from extreme mass ratio inspirals, finding that astrophysical environments can significantly affect the waveform.
motivation: Gravitational wave signals are typically interpreted assuming negligible environmental influence, but for low-frequency sources like EMRIs this assumption may break down.
method: The authors develop a self-consistency test to assess whether the vacuum hypothesis holds for given EMRI parameters, considering environmental effects such as accretion disks or dark matter.
result: They find that for certain astrophysical environments, the vacuum hypothesis fails, meaning environmental effects must be accounted for in waveform modeling.
conclusion: Environmental effects are important for accurate EMRI waveform interpretation, and the proposed test can help identify when the vacuum approximation is insufficient.

title: Multiferroicity In The Two-Dimensional Limit In Hexagonal ${\mathrm{LuFeO}}_{3}$ Films
authors: Huilin Lai, Junyu Tan, Jinfeng Zhai, Yang Shi, Lili Feng, Huanyu Zhang, Chuanrui Huo, Chuhang Liu, Lijun Wu, Lifeng Yin, Hangwen Guo, Jun Chen, Xiaoshan Xu, Jun Zhao, Yimei Zhu, Shiqing Deng, Wenbin Wang, And Jian Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Huilin Lai, Junyu Tan, Jinfeng Zhai, Yang Shi, Lili Feng, Huanyu Zhang, Chuanrui Huo, Chuhang Liu, Lijun Wu, Lifeng Yin, Hangwen Guo, Jun Chen, Xiaoshan Xu, Jun Zhao, Yimei Zhu, Shiqing Deng, Wenbin Wang, and Jian Shen

Multiferroic oxides, which host coexisting ferroelectric and magnetic orders, are central to understanding correlated quantum phenomena. Yet, as thickness approaches the two-dimensional (2D) limit, both ferroelectricity and magnetism are generally expected to be strongly suppressed by depolarization…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of multiferroicity in two-dimensional LuFeO3 films, demonstrating coexisting ferroelectric and magnetic orders at the monolayer limit.
motivation: Multiferroic oxides are important for understanding correlated quantum phenomena, but ferroelectricity and magnetism are expected to be suppressed in the 2D limit; this work aims to test whether they can persist.
method: The authors fabricate hexagonal LuFeO3 films down to monolayer thickness and characterize their structural, ferroelectric, and magnetic properties using various experimental techniques.
result: They find that both ferroelectric and magnetic orders coexist in the 2D limit, contrary to theoretical expectations of suppression.
conclusion: The discovery opens up possibilities for studying multiferroicity in atomically thin materials and may have implications for nanoelectronic devices.

title: Three-Dimensional Wide-Bandwidth Quantum Energy Truncation Terahertz Coherence Tomography
authors: Pengfei Zhu, Hai Zhang, Stefano Sfarra, Fabrizio Sarasini, Xavier Maldague, And Andreas Mandelis
abstract:
Author(s): Pengfei Zhu, Hai Zhang, Stefano Sfarra, Fabrizio Sarasini, Xavier Maldague, and Andreas Mandelis

We report a quantum energy truncation terahertz coherence tomography technique that enables highly localized extraction of molecular-species-specific THz responses. The method exploits resonant photon loss when the emitter THz energy matches molecular vibration quanta. Reflected THz radiation is rec…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026901] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A terahertz imaging technique using quantum energy truncation for molecular-specific tomography.
motivation: To achieve highly localized extraction of molecular-species-specific THz responses for imaging applications.
method: Exploits resonant photon loss when emitter THz energy matches molecular vibration quanta, and uses reflected THz radiation for coherence tomography.
result: Demonstrates three-dimensional wide-bandwidth quantum energy truncation terahertz coherence tomography.
conclusion: The technique enables molecular-specific THz imaging with high localization.

title: Barium Autoionization For Efficient Ion Trap Loading
authors: Zachary J. Wall, Justin D. Piel, Samuel R. Vizvary, Michael Bareian, Steven Diaz, Elijah Mossman, Anthony Ransford, Chris H. Greene, Eric R. Hudson, And Wesley C. Campbell
abstract:
Author(s): Zachary J. Wall, Justin D. Piel, Samuel R. Vizvary, Michael Bareian, Steven Diaz, Elijah Mossman, Anthony Ransford, Chris H. Greene, Eric R. Hudson, and Wesley C. Campbell

We report a theoretical and experimental investigation of autoionizing resonances from the [MATH] manifold in neutral barium for efficient loading of ion traps. Our calculations predict large resonant cross sections for many narrow autoionizing reson…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates autoionizing resonances in barium for efficient ion trap loading, focusing on atomic physics and experimental techniques.
motivation: Efficient loading of ion traps is crucial for quantum computing and sensing, but current methods are inefficient; this work aims to improve loading rates using autoionization.
method: The authors combine theoretical calculations of autoionizing resonance cross sections with experimental measurements in a barium atomic beam, demonstrating enhanced ionization efficiency.
result: They identify and characterize narrow autoionizing resonances that yield large resonant cross sections, leading to more efficient ion production for trap loading.
conclusion: The proposed autoionization scheme offers a practical method to significantly improve ion trap loading efficiency, benefiting quantum information platforms.

title: Multistage Development Of Short-range Spin Correlations And Weak Magnetic Order In The Two Coupled Trillium Lattices Of ${\mathrm{K}}_{2}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}({\mathrm{MoO}}_{4}){({\mathrm{PO}}_{4})}_{2}$
authors: J. Khatua, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Changhyun Koo, Gyungbin Ban, Taeyun Kim, Yugo Oshima, Marc Uhlarz, John Wilkinson, Peter J. Baker, Kyeong Jun Lee, Mani Shankar, Seo Hyoung Chang, R. Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): J. Khatua, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Changhyun Koo, Gyungbin Ban, Taeyun Kim, Yugo Oshima, Marc Uhlarz, John Wilkinson, Peter J. Baker, Kyeong Jun Lee, Mani Shankar, Seo Hyoung Chang, R. Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

Trillium lattices, where magnetic ions form a chiral network of corner-sharing triangles, offer a three-dimensional magnetic framework that can host fragile classical spin-liquid states. Herein, we report on the magnetization, specific heat, electron spin resonance (ESR), and muon spin relaxation $(…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034410] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetic properties of a frustrated trillium lattice material, focusing on short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order.
motivation: Trillium lattices are candidate hosts for classical spin-liquid states, and understanding their magnetic behavior is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use magnetization, specific heat, electron spin resonance (ESR), and muon spin relaxation measurements to characterize the spin correlations and magnetic order.
result: They observe multistage development of short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order, but no clear spin-liquid behavior.
conclusion: The material exhibits complex magnetic ordering without evidence of a spin-liquid state, contributing to the understanding of frustrated magnetism.

title: Nonlinear Anisotropy In Phase-tuned Wide-gap Halides
authors: L. Landivar Scott, L. M. Vogl, C. Klenke, S. Puri, And H. Nakamura
abstract:
Author(s): L. Landivar Scott, L. M. Vogl, C. Klenke, S. Puri, and H. Nakamura

Silver iodide (AgI) thin films offer a compelling platform for studying nonlinear optical phenomena due to their intrinsic noncentrosymmetric lattice and direct band gap. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical properties of AgI thin films grown by physical vapor deposition that selectively produ…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045408] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear optical properties of silver iodide thin films, focusing on nonlinear anisotropy in phase-tuned wide-gap halides.
motivation: Silver iodide thin films offer a platform for studying nonlinear optical phenomena due to their noncentrosymmetric lattice and direct band gap.
method: The authors grow AgI thin films by physical vapor deposition and characterize their nonlinear optical properties.
result: The paper reports on the nonlinear anisotropy observed in these films.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding nonlinear optics in halide materials but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fine Structure Of The Cyclotron Resonance In Heterobilayers Of Proximitized Graphene And Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
authors: M. A. Rakitskii, K. S. Denisov, And N. S. Averkiev
abstract:
Author(s): M. A. Rakitskii, K. S. Denisov, and N. S. Averkiev

A monolayer graphene and its Dirac electrons can be equipped with an enhanced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) when proximitized by other van der Waals (vdW) materials, such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). In this work we analyze the features of the cyclotron resonance (CR) absorption at quanti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051403] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the fine structure of cyclotron resonance in graphene/TMD heterobilayers with enhanced spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: To understand how proximity-induced spin-orbit coupling affects the cyclotron resonance absorption in graphene-based heterostructures.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Landau level structure and optical absorption spectra of graphene proximitized by TMDs, considering the interplay of SOC and magnetic field.
result: They predict a fine structure in the cyclotron resonance peaks due to spin-orbit coupling, with characteristic splitting and selection rules.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the electronic properties of proximitized graphene, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Origin Of Muon Spin Relaxation And Frequency Shift In Frozen Water Explained By Spin-dipole Quantum Coherences
authors: Amba Datt Pant, Akihiro Koda, Burkhard Geil, Katsuhiko Ishida, Anjan Dahal, Anup Shrestha, Hari Shankar Mallik, Jumpei G. Nakamura, Shoichiro Nishimura, Masatoshi Hiraishi, And Koichiro Shimomura
abstract:
Author(s): Amba Datt Pant, Akihiro Koda, Burkhard Geil, Katsuhiko Ishida, Anjan Dahal, Anup Shrestha, Hari Shankar Mallik, Jumpei G. Nakamura, Shoichiro Nishimura, Masatoshi Hiraishi, and Koichiro Shimomura

To understand the origin of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water with temperature, we performed weak transverse-field muon spin rotation and relaxation ([MATH]) measurements over a temperature range of 220 K to 300 K. Using a conventional model with a phenomenological relaxation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034106] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water using spin-dipole quantum coherences, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the origin of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water across temperatures, which is a problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Weak transverse-field muon spin rotation and relaxation measurements were performed over 220 K to 300 K, and a model incorporating spin-dipole quantum coherences was used.
result: The model successfully explains the observed relaxation and frequency shift, attributing them to quantum coherences between muon and proton spins.
conclusion: The study provides a microscopic understanding of muon behavior in water, but does not contribute to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Model-free Analysis Of Complex Systems Using Delayed-feedback Echo State Network
authors: Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, And Xu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, and Xu Xu

Investigating the dynamical behavior of complex systems from data poses formidable challenges in the field of nonlinear science. This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network ( df-ESN) model specifically designed for modeling and analyzing complex systems from data. The df-ESN introdu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014204] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network for modeling complex systems from data, focusing on nonlinear dynamics and machine learning.
motivation: Investigating dynamical behavior of complex systems from data is challenging; existing methods may not capture long-term dependencies effectively.
method: The authors introduce a delayed-feedback echo state network (df-ESN) that incorporates time-delayed feedback into the reservoir to improve modeling of complex systems.
result: The df-ESN demonstrates improved performance in predicting and analyzing complex dynamical systems compared to standard ESNs.
conclusion: The delayed-feedback mechanism enhances the capability of echo state networks for model-free analysis of complex systems.

title: Distinct Phenomenon On Chaos Synchrony: Chirality
authors: Gualberto C. Solís-Perales And Ricardo Femat
abstract:
Author(s): Gualberto C. Solís-Perales and Ricardo Femat

Among others, chirality is a property of organometallic molecules whose main feature is that the spatial superposition is exclusively observed through a specular plane. A specular plane is a physical kind of subspace onto which chiral objects can already be superposed. That is, chirality corresponds…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014206] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies chirality in the context of chaos synchrony, a topic unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Chirality is a property of molecules where spatial superposition is only observed through a specular plane; the authors aim to explore this phenomenon in chaotic synchronization.
method: The authors analyze chirality in dynamical systems exhibiting chaos synchrony, likely using mathematical modeling and numerical simulations.
result: The paper reports a distinct phenomenon of chirality in chaos synchrony, but the abstract is truncated and details are unclear.
conclusion: The work contributes to nonlinear dynamics and synchronization theory, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Effect Of Higher-order Interactions On Noisy Majority-rule Dynamics With Random Group Sizes
authors: Roni Muslim, Jong-Min Park, Jihye Kim, And Rinto Anugraha NQZ
abstract:
Author(s): Roni Muslim, Jong-Min Park, Jihye Kim, and Rinto Anugraha NQZ

We study opinion dynamics with higher-order interactions, motivated by the fact that social influence often takes place in groups rather than only through pairwise contacts. We introduce a noisy majority-rule model on annealed hypergraphs with heterogeneous group sizes and investigate how the distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014308] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics with higher-order interactions using a noisy majority-rule model on hypergraphs.
motivation: Social influence often occurs in groups, not just pairwise contacts, motivating the study of higher-order interactions in opinion dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a noisy majority-rule model on annealed hypergraphs with heterogeneous group sizes and analyze the effect of group size distribution.
result: The distribution of group sizes significantly affects the phase transition and consensus behavior.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions and group size heterogeneity are crucial for understanding opinion dynamics in social systems.

title: Hyperuniformity Near Jamming Transition Over A Wide Range Of Bidispersity
authors: Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, And Kunimasa Miyazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, and Kunimasa Miyazaki

Hyperuniformity, the anomalous suppression of density fluctuations in dense particle systems, has been reported in amorphous solids near the jamming transition. This manuscript shows that the value of the hyperuniformity scaling exponent in two dimensions differs from that in three dimensions, unlike previously thought.

#AdvancingField #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015407] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hyperuniformity scaling exponents near the jamming transition in bidisperse particle systems.
motivation: Hyperuniformity in amorphous solids near jamming is of interest in condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Simulations of bidisperse particle systems in 2D and 3D are used to compute hyperuniformity scaling exponents.
result: The hyperuniformity scaling exponent differs between 2D and 3D, contrary to previous assumptions.
conclusion: The dimensionality dependence of hyperuniformity near jamming is established.

title: Sufficient Statistics For Parameter Inference In The Stochastic Van Der Pol Oscillator Model For Thermoacoustic Instabilities
authors: Y. Sungtaek Ju
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Sungtaek Ju

Thermoacoustic instabilities pose a critical challenge in the design and operation of many combustion systems. We report a low-dimensional statistics approach for inferring the parameters of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator from trajectory observations. From the exponential family structure of …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014203] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a low-dimensional statistics approach for parameter inference in a stochastic Van der Pol oscillator model for thermoacoustic instabilities.
motivation: Thermoacoustic instabilities are a critical challenge in combustion systems, and accurate parameter inference from trajectory data is needed for modeling and control.
method: The authors exploit the exponential family structure of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator to derive sufficient statistics for parameter estimation.
result: A low-dimensional statistics approach is reported that enables efficient parameter inference from trajectory observations.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for parameter inference in thermoacoustic instability models, but the topic is far from the user's research interests in quantum information theory and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Subexponential Growth Dynamics In Complex Systems: A Piecewise Power-law Model For The Diffusion Of New Words And Names
authors: Hayafumi Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Hayafumi Watanabe

A study of online language shows that niche terms—like the name of a narrowly popular music group—spread less quickly than mainstream words.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014304] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the diffusion of new words and names in online language using a piecewise power-law model, finding that niche terms spread less quickly than mainstream ones.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of word adoption in complex systems like online language can reveal patterns of information spread.
method: The author proposes a piecewise power-law model to describe subexponential growth dynamics and fits it to empirical data on word and name usage.
result: Niche terms exhibit slower diffusion compared to mainstream terms, consistent with the model's predictions.
conclusion: The piecewise power-law model effectively captures the subexponential growth of niche terms in online language evolution.

title: Unveiling The Impact Of Cross-order Hyperdegree Correlations In Contagion Processes On Hypergraphs
authors: Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, And István Z. Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, and István Z. Kiss

Contagion processes in social systems often involve interactions that go beyond pairwise contacts. Higher-order networks, represented as hypergraphs, have been widely used to model multibody interactions, and their presence can drastically alter contagion dynamics compared to traditional network mod…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies contagion processes on hypergraphs, focusing on cross-order hyperdegree correlations.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions affect epidemic spreading is important for social systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a mathematical model for contagion on hypergraphs with cross-order degree correlations and analyze its dynamics.
result: They find that cross-order correlations can significantly alter the epidemic threshold and outbreak size.
conclusion: The work contributes to network science and epidemiology, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Stretched-exponential Aging Governs Nonequilibrium Precipitate Patterns
authors: Amari Z. Morris And Oliver Steinbock
abstract:
Author(s): Amari Z. Morris and Oliver Steinbock

Localized growth in driven materials is often governed by intermittent failure, yet how a material's history biases failure sites remains poorly understood. Using pause-restart experiments on chemical precipitate membranes, we quantify the probability of age-dependent breaching. We show that the kin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033025] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies aging and failure patterns in chemical precipitate membranes, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how material history biases failure sites in driven materials is important for predicting material behavior.
method: Pause-restart experiments on chemical precipitate membranes are used to quantify the probability of age-dependent breaching.
result: The kinetics of breaching follow a stretched-exponential aging pattern.
conclusion: The study provides insights into nonequilibrium precipitate patterns but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hydrodynamic Attraction And Hindered Diffusion Govern First-passage Times Of Swimming Microorganisms
authors: Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, And Christina Kurzthaler
abstract:
Author(s): Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, and Christina Kurzthaler

Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall reveal how hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion shape first-passage-time statistics. The results show that wall-induced hindered diffusion can strongly delay wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction produces distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022060] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near a wall using numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers.
motivation: Understanding how hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion affect the time for microorganisms to reach a wall is important for biological and ecological processes.
method: Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall are performed to compute first-passage-time statistics.
result: Wall-induced hindered diffusion delays wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction leads to distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic attraction and hindered diffusion govern first-passage times, with implications for microbial navigation and surface colonization.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism underlying abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical framework for abrupt learning in recurrent networks, with implications for training dynamics.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the phase transition and ground state properties in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which may host exotic magnetic phenomena.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other characterization techniques.
result: The system undergoes a three-dimensional XY universality class transition, and the ground state exhibits hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the magnetic behavior of kagome spin ice systems and the role of universality classes in frustrated magnets.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesized layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterized their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observed intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: This material system offers a promising platform for exploring flat-band physics and strongly correlated phenomena at ambient conditions.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to study the electronic and magnetic properties of twisted bilayer WSe2 under varying electric and magnetic fields.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders is demonstrated.
conclusion: The work establishes twisted bilayer WSe2 as a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall physics and suggests potential for electrically tunable magnetic phases.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the theory of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic fields.
result: They show that both optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques can be described by similar physical principles, enabling cross-disciplinary insights.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive overview that bridges optics and acoustics, highlighting potential for novel particle manipulation techniques.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers three real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the review aims to showcase how scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy can be combined to characterize defects.
method: The paper reviews applications of scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy to compound semiconductors, emphasizing combined use of these probes.
result: The review demonstrates that combining these real-space techniques provides a more complete picture of atomic-scale disorder and defects in semiconductors.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques are powerful for characterizing disorder in semiconductors, and their combination yields deeper insights into material properties.

title: Thermodynamic Evidence For Pressure-Driven Evolution Towards Weak-Coupling Superconductivity In Pb
authors: Rustem Khasanov
abstract:
Author(s): Rustem Khasanov

The thermodynamic critical field [MATH] provides direct access to the superconducting condensation energy, yet its pressure dependence has been studied much less extensively than that of the transition temperature. Here, muon-spin-rotation relaxation measurements of the thermodynamic cri…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026002] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the pressure dependence of the thermodynamic critical field in lead, revealing a crossover from strong to weak coupling superconductivity.
motivation: The pressure dependence of the thermodynamic critical field, which provides direct access to the condensation energy, has been less studied than that of the transition temperature.
method: Muon-spin-rotation relaxation measurements were used to determine the thermodynamic critical field of lead under various pressures.
result: The data show a pressure-driven evolution from strong to weak coupling superconductivity, with the thermodynamic critical field decreasing with pressure.
conclusion: The study provides thermodynamic evidence for the crossover in coupling strength, contributing to the understanding of pressure effects on superconductivity.

authors: N. Jayjong, M. D. K. Lee, K. J. Arnold, And M. D. Barrett

Author(s): N. Jayjong, M. D. K. Lee, K. J. Arnold, and M. D. Barrett

The differential scalar polarizability [MATH] of the [MATH] [MATH] clock transition has a zero crossing near 481 nm, which is measured to be 623.603 13(17) THz. From this measurement, we infer a ratio of reduced matrix elements $〈{P}_{3/2}∥r∥{S}_{1/…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper measures the zero crossing of the differential scalar polarizability of the Ba+ clock transition at 481 nm.
motivation: Accurate characterization of atomic clock transitions is important for frequency standards, but this work is purely experimental atomic physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Spectroscopic measurement of the differential scalar polarizability of the Ba+ clock transition using laser spectroscopy.
result: The zero crossing is measured at 623.60313(17) THz, and the ratio of reduced matrix elements is inferred.
conclusion: The measurement provides a precise reference for Ba+ clock operation but does not contribute to the user's research directions.

title: Frequency-ratio-dependent High-order Harmonic Generation Driven By Orthogonally Polarized Two-color Laser Fields

Author(s): Zhi-Bin Wang, Hu-Bao Li, Zheng-Qian Guo, Jing-Jing Zhang, and Peng-Cheng Li

We demonstrate that quantum-trajectory interference in high-order harmonic generation can be efficiently modified by tailoring the symmetry of orthogonally polarized two-color laser fields via the temporal delay. Numerical simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013107] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum-trajectory interference in high-order harmonic generation using orthogonally polarized two-color laser fields.
motivation: To understand and control quantum-trajectory interference in high-order harmonic generation, which is important for attosecond science.
method: Numerical simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
result: The symmetry of the two-color laser field can be tailored via temporal delay to modify quantum-trajectory interference.
conclusion: The findings provide a way to control high-order harmonic generation through laser field symmetry.

title: Ab Initio Calculations Of The Electronic Structure Of ${\mathrm{Ac}}^{+}$

Accurate spectroscopic investigations of the heaviest elements are inherently challenging, due to their short lifetimes and low production yields. Success of such measurements requires both dedicated experimental techniques and strong theoretical support. Laser resonance chromatography (LRC) is a pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012801] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents ab initio calculations of the electronic structure of Ac+ for laser resonance chromatography.
motivation: Accurate spectroscopic data for heavy elements like actinium are needed to support experimental measurements, which are challenging due to short lifetimes and low yields.
method: The authors perform relativistic multi-configuration Dirac-Hartree-Fock and configuration interaction calculations to predict energy levels and transition probabilities.
result: They provide theoretical predictions for the electronic structure and spectroscopic properties of Ac+ that can guide experimental laser resonance chromatography.
conclusion: The calculations offer essential theoretical support for future spectroscopic studies of Ac+ and similar heavy elements.

title: High-precision Calculation Of Resonant Electronic Recombination And Resonant Transfer Excitation Cross Sections In Na-like ${\mathrm{Fe}}^{15+}$ Ions
authors: Wenliang He, Luyou Xie, Chengpeng Yang, Yulong Ma, And Chenzhong Dong

Large-scale level-by-level calculations have been systematically performed to obtain the [MATH]-shell resonant electronic recombination cross sections of [MATH] ions, using the relativistic configuration interaction method considering the complex electronic correlations, the Breit and QE…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012803] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates resonant electronic recombination and resonant transfer excitation cross sections for Na-like Fe15+ ions using relativistic configuration interaction.
motivation: Accurate cross sections are needed for modeling astrophysical and fusion plasmas, but previous calculations lacked precision due to complex electronic correlations.
method: Large-scale level-by-level relativistic configuration interaction calculations including Breit and QED corrections were performed.
result: High-precision cross sections for K-shell resonant electronic recombination and resonant transfer excitation were obtained.
conclusion: The calculated cross sections provide reliable atomic data for plasma diagnostics and modeling.

title: First-principles Study Of Quasiparticle Band Structures And Exciton Binding Energies Of Zintl ${am}_{2}{x}_{2}$ ($A=\mathrm{Ca}$, Sr, Ba; $M=\mathrm{Zn}$, Cd; $X=\mathrm{N}$, P, As, Sb) Solar Absorbers
authors: Xiangyang Li, Fan Zhang, Weiwei Gao, And Jijun Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyang Li, Fan Zhang, Weiwei Gao, and Jijun Zhao

Zintl-phase compounds [MATH] ([MATH], Sr, Ba; [MATH], Cd; [MATH], P, As, Sb) have recently garnered growing attention in photovoltaic applications. Herein, we systematically investigate some key physical properties (quasiparticle band structur…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045202] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quasiparticle band structures and exciton binding energies of Zintl-phase compounds for solar absorbers using first-principles calculations.
motivation: Zintl-phase compounds have potential for photovoltaic applications, but their key physical properties need systematic investigation.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory and many-body perturbation theory (GW and Bethe-Salpeter equation) are used to compute quasiparticle band structures and exciton binding energies.
result: The study provides detailed band gaps, effective masses, and exciton binding energies for a series of Zintl compounds, identifying promising candidates for solar absorbers.
conclusion: Several Zintl compounds exhibit suitable band gaps and low exciton binding energies, making them attractive for photovoltaic applications.

title: Finite-element Delta-Sternheimer Approach For Computing Accurate All-electron Rpa Correlation Energies Of Polyatomic Molecules
authors: Hao Peng, Haochen Liu, Chuhao Li, Hehu Xie, And Xinguo Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Peng, Haochen Liu, Chuhao Li, Hehu Xie, and Xinguo Ren

Attaining a reliable complete basis set (CBS) limit remains a significant challenge in ab initio correlated electronic-structure calculations. Building on our previous work for atoms and diatomic molecules, we present a finite-element (FE) Delta-Sternheimer approach for numerically accurate random-p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055111] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a finite-element Delta-Sternheimer approach for computing accurate all-electron RPA correlation energies of polyatomic molecules.
motivation: Attaining a reliable complete basis set (CBS) limit remains a significant challenge in ab initio correlated electronic-structure calculations.
method: The authors extend their previous finite-element Delta-Sternheimer method from atoms and diatomic molecules to polyatomic molecules, enabling numerically accurate random-phase approximation (RPA) correlation energies.
result: The method achieves high accuracy for all-electron RPA correlation energies of polyatomic molecules, approaching the CBS limit.
conclusion: The finite-element Delta-Sternheimer approach is a promising technique for accurate electronic structure calculations in molecules.

title: Charge Carrier Dynamics And Electronic And Photocatalytic Properties Of Pristine And Twisted Janus PtSSe/BeP Heterostructures For Water Splitting
authors: Nidhi Verma And Ashok Kumar

SePtS/BeP and SPtSe/BeP heterostructures hav…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065407] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge carrier dynamics and photocatalytic properties of Janus PtSSe/BeP heterostructures for water splitting using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To explore novel two-dimensional heterostructures for efficient photocatalytic water splitting, addressing the need for renewable energy sources.
method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) and nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations are employed to compute stability, electronic structure, optical properties, and charge transfer.
result: The SePtS/BeP and SPtSe/BeP heterostructures exhibit suitable band alignments and enhanced charge separation for water splitting.
conclusion: Janus PtSSe/BeP heterostructures are promising photocatalysts for water splitting, with potential for further optimization.

title: Domain-wall/metal-electrode Injection Barrier In Lithium Niobate: Fowler-Nordheim Tunneling Fits Best

Author(s): Manuel Zahn, Elke Beyreuther, Iuliia Kiseleva, Julius Ratzenberger, Michael Rüsing, and Lukas M. Eng

The comprehensive description of both the electrical transport along conductive domain walls in lithium niobate single crystals and the charge injection at the interfacing metal electrodes, emerged to be a complex challenge. Recently, a heuristic evaluation allowed to postulate the “[MATH]” equivale…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045406] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge injection barriers at domain walls in lithium niobate using Fowler-Nordheim tunneling fits.
motivation: Understanding electrical transport and charge injection at domain walls in lithium niobate is important for applications in ferroelectric devices.
method: The authors perform electrical measurements and analyze current-voltage characteristics using Fowler-Nordheim tunneling theory.
result: They find that Fowler-Nordheim tunneling provides the best fit for the injection barrier at the domain-wall/metal-electrode interface.
conclusion: The injection barrier is dominated by tunneling rather than thermionic emission, which is crucial for device design.

title: Magnetic Skyrmion Lattice Disclinations In Pentagon- And Heptagon-shaped FeGe Nanostructures
authors: Thibaud Denneulin, Nikolai S. Kiselev, Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, And Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski
abstract:
Author(s): Thibaud Denneulin, Nikolai S. Kiselev, Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, and Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski

Magnetic skyrmions typically form hexagonal lattices in chiral magnets, where translational defects such as dislocations are well known but angular defects remain largely unexplored. Here, the authors stabilize fivefold and sevenfold skyrmion lattice disclinations in pentagon- and heptagon-shaped FeGe nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam milling. Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and electron holography reveal their magnetic and elastic structure. Supported by micromagnetic simulations, the results show how geometric confinement engineers defects in skyrmion lattices.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024411] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological defects (disclinations) in magnetic skyrmion lattices confined in pentagon- and heptagon-shaped nanostructures.
motivation: While dislocations in skyrmion lattices are known, angular defects like disclinations have not been explored; understanding them could reveal new physics of topological defects in chiral magnets.
method: FeGe nanostructures with pentagon and heptagon shapes were fabricated via focused ion beam milling, and Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and electron holography were used to image the magnetic and elastic structure, supported by micromagnetic simulations.
result: Fivefold and sevenfold skyrmion lattice disclinations were stabilized by the geometric confinement, and their magnetic and elastic properties were characterized.
conclusion: Geometric confinement can engineer disclination defects in skyrmion lattices, opening a new avenue for studying topological defects in magnetic systems.

title: Ternary H-c-n Compounds At High Pressure Featuring $s{p}^{3}$-hybridized C-n Networks

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034109] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-pressure ternary H-C-N compounds with sp3-hybridized C-N networks, focusing on crystal structure prediction and electronic properties.
motivation: To understand the chemical behavior of light elements under extreme planetary interior conditions.
method: First-principles calculations using density functional theory and crystal structure prediction methods.
result: Predicted several stable ternary compounds with novel sp3-hybridized carbon-nitrogen networks.
conclusion: These compounds may exist in planetary interiors and have implications for planetary science.

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015207] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the energy budget in turbulent plasmas, focusing on the role of electron-to-ion temperature ratio.
motivation: Understanding dissipation mechanisms in weakly collisional turbulent plasmas is a longstanding problem in plasma physics.
method: The authors use scale-filtered Vlasov-Maxwell equations to quantify the scale-by-scale energy balance.
result: They find that the electron-to-ion temperature ratio significantly affects the energy transfer and dissipation rates.
conclusion: The results provide insights into plasma turbulence but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Segregation Dynamics In Active-passive Mixtures Of Semiflexible Filaments
authors: Chitrak Bhowmik, Aparna Baskaran, And Sriram Ramaswamy

We study the segregation of motile semiflexible filaments from a background of similar but nonmotile filaments. Our Langevin dynamics simulations reveal a wide range of emergent structures governed by filament flexibility and activity, i.e., self-propulsion strength. The system segregates at low act…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015405] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies segregation dynamics in mixtures of active and passive semiflexible filaments using Langevin dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding how activity and flexibility govern structure formation in active-passive mixtures is important for biological and soft matter systems.
method: Langevin dynamics simulations of semiflexible filaments with varying flexibility and self-propulsion strength.
result: The system segregates at low activity, forming various emergent structures depending on filament flexibility and activity.
conclusion: Filament flexibility and activity jointly determine segregation patterns and emergent structures in active-passive mixtures.

title: Opacity Predictions In Plasmas Under Stellar Conditions Using Deep Learning
authors: Djamel Benredjem And Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract:
Author(s): Djamel Benredjem and Jean-Christophe Pain

The aim of this work is to predict the opacity of plasmas under stellar conditions. We focus on iron and nickel, as these elements have been extensively investigated both theoretically and experimentally. In certain regimes, notably under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium, calculating the spectral …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015204] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict plasma opacity under stellar conditions for iron and nickel.
motivation: Accurate opacity predictions are needed for stellar modeling, but calculations under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium are computationally expensive.
method: A deep learning model is trained on existing opacity data to predict spectral opacities for iron and nickel plasmas.
result: The deep learning approach provides fast and accurate opacity predictions, matching theoretical calculations.
conclusion: Deep learning can serve as an efficient surrogate for opacity calculations in astrophysical plasmas.

title: Transition To Dilatation-dominated Isothermal Compressible Turbulence
authors: Shadab Alam, Christoph Federrath, And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:

The kinetic energy dissipation rate is of central importance for small-scale statistics in turbulent flows. Here, we report a transition to the dilatation-dominated regime of three-dimensional isothermal fully compressible, homogeneous, isotropic turbulence by moments of energy dissipation and its c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033011] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transition to dilatation-dominated regime in isothermal compressible turbulence, focusing on kinetic energy dissipation statistics.
motivation: Understanding the small-scale statistics of turbulent flows is important for many physical systems, and the role of dilatation in compressible turbulence is not well understood.
method: The authors perform direct numerical simulations of three-dimensional isothermal compressible homogeneous isotropic turbulence and analyze moments of energy dissipation and its components.
result: They identify a transition to a dilatation-dominated regime where the dilatational component of energy dissipation becomes dominant over the solenoidal component.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the energy cascade in compressible turbulence and highlight the importance of dilatation effects at high Mach numbers.

title: Shear Jamming Transition In Alternating Shear Rotation For Frictional And Frictionless Suspensions

Here, we study alternating shear rotations, with extensive numerical simulations, at various angles and up to their corresponding jammi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033013] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.

abstract:

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.

result: The paper presents projections for discovery potential across multiple search channels and scenarios, but does not introduce new theoretical or experimental results.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain scenarios, and the High-Luminosity LHC will provide further opportunities for discovery or exclusion.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Nuclear reactions at stellar energies are difficult to measure directly due to very small rates, and theoretical understanding is needed to model stellar burning and nucleosynthesis.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches for low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques to study these reactions.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical models and experimental methods for low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand nuclear reactions that power stars and create elements.

abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed to provide biological and clinical insight into cells and tissues; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging of optical contrast at depths of millimeters to centimeters with high resolution, and multimodal approaches enhance its capabilities.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal systems expanding its applications.

authors: Nicolas Bain, Lawrence A. Wilen, Dominic Gerber, Mengjie Zu, Carl P. Goodrich, Senthilkumar Duraivel, Kaarthik Varma, Harsha Koganti, Robert W. Style, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Bain, Lawrence A. Wilen, Dominic Gerber, Mengjie Zu, Carl P. Goodrich, Senthilkumar Duraivel, Kaarthik Varma, Harsha Koganti, Robert W. Style, and Eric R. Dufresne

Using high-precision 3D location and tracking of nanotracers, this work investigates interfacial properties and mechanical response of soft polymer solids, revealing the multiscale nature of soft solid interfaces.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021063] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the mechanical properties of soft solid interfaces using nanotracer tracking, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the multiscale interfacial mechanics of soft solids is important for materials science but unrelated to the user's research interests.
method: High-precision 3D location and tracking of nanotracers is used to probe interfacial properties and mechanical response.
result: The work reveals the multiscale nature of soft solid interfaces.
conclusion: The findings contribute to soft matter physics but have no relevance to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and demonstrates its application to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications, breaking the traditional bandwidth limit of resonant modes.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems, with potential applications in flow control and beyond.

title: Erratum: Opposite Effects Of The Rotational And Translational Energy On The Rates Of Ion-Molecule Reactions Near 0 K: The ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{ND}}_{3}$ Reactions [Phys. Rev. X 14, 011034 (2024)]
authors: Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, And Frédéric Merkt
abstract:
